subjects.title: System Design
subjects.description: Design large-scale systems: from latency and caching to consensus, streaming and full case studies.

modules.title: Fundamentals
modules.summary: The core vocabulary and reasoning tools of system design: requirements, latency, availability, scalability, estimation, CAP/PACELC and trade-offs.

lessons.title: What system design is and how to approach a problem
lessons.summary: System design turns fuzzy goals into an architecture by pinning down functional requirements, non-functional requirements and constraints first.

lessons.title: Latency, throughput and percentiles
lessons.summary: How long one request takes versus how many you can handle, why p99 matters more than the average, and the latency numbers every engineer should know.

lessons.title: Availability, reliability and the maths of nines
lessons.summary: What "four nines" really allows, how to calculate availability for components in series and in parallel, and how MTBF and MTTR drive it.

lessons.title: Scalability, statelessness, Amdahl's and Little's laws
lessons.summary: Vertical vs horizontal scaling, why stateless services scale easily and stateful ones don't, and two laws that bound what scaling can achieve.

lessons.title: Back-of-the-envelope estimation
lessons.summary: Turn users and behaviours into QPS, storage, bandwidth and memory figures in minutes, with full worked examples you can reuse.

lessons.title: CAP and PACELC, and what they really mean
lessons.summary: What the CAP theorem actually proves, why "pick two of three" is misleading, and how PACELC adds the latency trade-off that matters every day.

lessons.title: Thinking in trade-offs
lessons.summary: The recurring trade-offs behind every design decision (consistency vs availability, latency vs durability, cost, complexity, build vs buy) and how to reason about them explicitly.

modules.title: Networking & Traffic
modules.summary: How a request actually travels: DNS, TCP/UDP, HTTP versions, TLS, load balancers, proxies, CDNs and global traffic routing.

lessons.title: What happens when you type a URL
lessons.summary: The full journey of a web request, from parsing the URL through DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP to rendering, and where the time goes.

lessons.title: DNS: resolution, records, TTLs and traffic steering
lessons.summary: How DNS resolution really works, the record types you'll use, how TTLs and caching shape failover, and how DNS doubles as a load balancer.

lessons.title: TCP vs UDP, and HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
lessons.summary: What TCP and UDP guarantee, how each HTTP version uses connections, and why head-of-line blocking drove the move to QUIC.

lessons.title: TLS and HTTPS: handshakes, certificates and termination
lessons.summary: What a TLS handshake does and costs, how certificate trust works, where to terminate TLS in your architecture, and how to claw back handshake latency.

lessons.title: Load balancers: L4 vs L7, algorithms and health checks
lessons.summary: How load balancers spread traffic, the difference between L4 and L7, which algorithm to pick and why, and how health checks and sticky sessions go wrong.

lessons.title: Reverse proxies, API gateways and service meshes
lessons.summary: What reverse proxies, API gateways and service meshes each do, where they sit, how they overlap, and when each one is worth its cost.

lessons.title: CDNs: edge caching, cache keys and origin shielding
lessons.summary: How CDNs work, push vs pull, designing cache keys, tiered caching and origin shields, and how CDNs speed up even uncacheable dynamic content.

lessons.title: Global traffic management: GeoDNS, anycast and failover
lessons.summary: How to steer users to the right region with GeoDNS, latency-based routing and anycast, and how to fail over between regions without making things worse.

modules.title: Caching
modules.summary: Where caches live, how to read and write through them, eviction, invalidation, HTTP caching, distributed caches and the failure modes that take systems down.

lessons.title: Why cache, and where
lessons.summary: What a cache buys you, the layers it can live in from browser to buffer pool, and the hit-ratio maths that tells you whether it is working.

lessons.title: Caching strategies
lessons.summary: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back and write-around — how data flows between app, cache and database, and what each costs.

lessons.title: Eviction policies
lessons.summary: LRU, LFU, FIFO and TTL, how to implement them, and the cheap approximations that Redis, Memcached, Caffeine and Linux actually use.

lessons.title: Invalidation and consistency
lessons.summary: Why caches serve stale data, the race conditions between database and cache writes, and the tools that tame them — delete over update, versioning, leases and change data capture.

lessons.title: HTTP caching
lessons.summary: How browsers, proxies and CDNs decide what to store and for how long — Cache-Control, validators (ETag, Last-Modified), Vary and stale-while-revalidate.

lessons.title: Distributed caching
lessons.summary: Redis versus Memcached, spreading keys across nodes with consistent hashing and hash slots, and what replication and persistence do (and don't) protect you from.

lessons.title: Cache failure modes
lessons.summary: Stampedes, hot keys, penetration, avalanches and cold starts — how caches take systems down, and the coalescing, early-expiry, Bloom-filter and warming techniques that stop them.

modules.title: Databases & Storage
modules.summary: How databases store, index, replicate and partition data, what transactions really guarantee, and how to pick the right one.

lessons.title: Relational databases and ACID
lessons.summary: Tables, schemas, keys and joins, what ACID actually promises, and when to normalise or denormalise.

lessons.title: NoSQL families
lessons.summary: Key-value, document, wide-column, graph, time-series and search stores, what each is built for, and real examples.

lessons.title: Indexing
lessons.summary: B-trees versus LSM trees, composite and covering indexes, and what every index costs on writes.

lessons.title: Transactions and isolation levels
lessons.summary: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantoms and write skew, and how MVCC, snapshot isolation, 2PL and SSI prevent them.

lessons.title: Replication
lessons.summary: Single-leader, multi-leader and leaderless replication, sync versus async, replication lag anomalies and failover.

lessons.title: Partitioning and sharding
lessons.summary: Range versus hash partitioning, consistent hashing, hot spots, secondary indexes on sharded data, rebalancing and resharding.

lessons.title: Choosing a database
lessons.summary: Pick a database from access patterns, consistency needs, scale and operational cost, and know when to use several.

lessons.title: Storage engine internals
lessons.summary: Write-ahead logs, pages, compaction, read/write/space amplification, bloom filters, and why analytics uses column stores.

modules.title: Distributed Systems & Consensus
modules.summary: Partial failure, consistency models, time and ordering, quorums, Raft and Paxos, locks and fencing, distributed transactions, CRDTs and gossip.

lessons.title: Why distributed systems are hard
lessons.summary: Partial failure, unreliable networks and clocks, the eight fallacies, and why the Two Generals problem has no solution.

lessons.title: Consistency models
lessons.summary: What linearizable, sequential, causal and eventual consistency actually promise, plus the session guarantees users notice.

lessons.title: Time and ordering
lessons.summary: Why wall clocks lie, how NTP works, and how Lamport clocks, vector clocks, hybrid logical clocks and TrueTime order events.

lessons.title: Quorums and Dynamo-style replication
lessons.summary: N, R and W; why R + W > N isn't the whole story; sloppy quorums, hinted handoff, read repair and Merkle-tree anti-entropy.

lessons.title: Consensus, Raft and Paxos
lessons.summary: What consensus is, why FLP says it can't always terminate, how Raft elects leaders and replicates logs safely, Paxos in outline, and etcd and ZooKeeper.

lessons.title: Leader election, leases and distributed locks
lessons.summary: Why every distributed lock is really a lease, how fencing tokens stop stale holders doing damage, and the Redlock debate.

lessons.title: Distributed transactions and sagas
lessons.summary: Two-phase commit and why it blocks, three-phase commit's limits, and sagas with orchestration, choreography and compensating actions.

lessons.title: Conflict resolution, CRDTs and gossip
lessons.summary: Resolving concurrent writes with last-write-wins, version vectors and CRDTs (G-Counter, PN-Counter, OR-Set), and spreading state with gossip, phi accrual and SWIM.

modules.title: Messaging & Streaming
modules.summary: Queues, pub/sub, Kafka, delivery guarantees, event-driven architecture and stream processing: how services talk asynchronously, reliably and at scale.

lessons.title: Synchronous vs asynchronous communication
lessons.summary: Why systems put a queue between services, what decoupling really buys you, and how a queue absorbs traffic spikes.

lessons.title: Message queues: competing consumers, acks and DLQs
lessons.summary: How point-to-point queues hand each message to one worker, and how acknowledgements, visibility timeouts and dead-letter queues keep work from being lost.

lessons.title: Publish/subscribe and fan-out
lessons.summary: Topics and subscriptions, the SNS-to-SQS fan-out pattern, message filtering, and when consumers should be pushed messages or pull them.

lessons.title: Log-based streaming: Kafka in depth
lessons.summary: How Kafka's partitioned, replicated log works: offsets, consumer groups, retention, compaction, ISR replication and exactly what ordering it guarantees.

lessons.title: Delivery semantics and idempotent consumers
lessons.summary: At-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once explained honestly, with idempotent consumers, deduplication and how Kafka transactions really work.

lessons.title: Ordering, retries, backpressure and lag
lessons.summary: How to keep per-entity ordering without killing parallelism, handle poison messages in ordered streams, and stop a slow consumer from sinking the system.

lessons.title: Event-driven architecture, outbox and CDC
lessons.summary: Event notification vs event-carried state transfer, event sourcing and CQRS, and how the transactional outbox and change data capture solve the dual-write problem.

lessons.title: Stream processing: windows, time and state
lessons.summary: How stream processors such as Flink and Kafka Streams compute over unbounded data: event time vs processing time, windows, watermarks, late data and fault-tolerant state.

modules.title: API Design
modules.summary: Design APIs that are clear, evolvable, safe to retry and hard to abuse: REST, GraphQL and gRPC, pagination, idempotency, rate limiting, auth, real-time and webhooks.

lessons.title: REST fundamentals
lessons.summary: Resources, HTTP methods and their safety and idempotency, status codes, and why statelessness lets REST APIs scale.

lessons.title: REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC
lessons.summary: Three API styles compared, including over-fetching, the N+1 problem, protobuf encoding, streaming and how to choose.

lessons.title: Designing good APIs
lessons.summary: Pagination (offset vs cursor), filtering and sorting, versioning, consistent error formats, and how to evolve an API without breaking clients.

lessons.title: Idempotency and safe retries
lessons.summary: How idempotency keys make POST safe to retry, how Stripe implements them, and how to combine retries with backoff and jitter.

lessons.title: Rate limiting
lessons.summary: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed and sliding windows, distributed rate limiting with Redis, and how to signal limits with 429 and Retry-After.

lessons.title: Authentication and authorisation
lessons.summary: Sessions vs tokens, JWTs and their pitfalls, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows, API keys, mTLS, and RBAC vs ABAC.

lessons.title: Real-time communication
lessons.summary: Short polling, long polling, Server-Sent Events and WebSockets compared, and how to scale millions of persistent connections.

lessons.title: Webhooks, API gateways and BFFs
lessons.summary: Delivering webhooks reliably and securely (signing, retries, ordering, replay protection), and what API gateways and backends-for-frontends do in practice.

modules.title: Architecture & Scaling Patterns
modules.summary: How real systems are carved into services and scaled: monoliths vs microservices, stateless tiers, discovery, read and write scaling, object storage, search, batch and stream processing, and multi-region designs.

lessons.title: Monoliths, modular monoliths and microservices
lessons.summary: How to decide where the boundaries between deployable units go, why Conway's law matters, and how to avoid building a distributed monolith.

lessons.title: Stateless services and scaling the web tier
lessons.summary: Why stateless application servers are the foundation of horizontal scaling, where session state goes instead, and how autoscaling, containers and Kubernetes fit together.

lessons.title: Service discovery and inter-service communication
lessons.summary: How services find each other when instances come and go, what sidecars and service meshes add, and when to call synchronously versus send a message.

lessons.title: Scaling reads
lessons.summary: The toolbox for read-heavy systems, from read replicas and cache layers to denormalisation, materialised views and precomputed results, and the consistency costs of each.

lessons.title: Scaling writes
lessons.summary: Why writes are harder to scale than reads, and the architectural patterns that help, including sharding, batching, queues as shock absorbers, append-only designs and hot-partition mitigation.

lessons.title: Blob storage, uploads and media pipelines
lessons.summary: How S3-style object storage works and why it differs from file systems and databases, how presigned URLs and multipart uploads keep big files off your servers, and how video transcoding pipelines are built.

lessons.title: Search systems
lessons.summary: How full-text search works under the hood, from tokenisation and inverted indexes to TF-IDF and BM25 ranking, how Elasticsearch distributes it with shards and replicas, and how to keep a search index in sync with your database.

lessons.title: Batch and stream data processing
lessons.summary: How large-scale data processing works, from MapReduce and Spark to stream processors, why Lambda and Kappa architectures exist, and how data lakes, warehouses and lakehouses fit together.

lessons.title: Multi-region and geo-distributed architecture
lessons.summary: Why and how systems span several regions, the trade-offs between active-passive and active-active, data residency constraints, handling write conflicts, and limiting blast radius with cell-based architecture.

modules.title: Reliability, Operations & Security
modules.summary: Design for failure, survive overload and disasters, observe and measure what users feel, ship safely, and secure the whole system.

lessons.title: Designing for failure
lessons.summary: Classify how components fail, find single points of failure, contain the blast radius and use redundancy that actually helps.

lessons.title: Timeouts, retries, backoff and jitter
lessons.summary: Set timeouts from latency data, retry only what's safe, add exponential backoff with jitter, and stop retry storms with budgets.

lessons.title: Circuit breakers, bulkheads and load shedding
lessons.summary: Stop failures spreading with circuit breakers and bulkheads, and survive overload with load shedding, backpressure and graceful degradation.

lessons.title: Disaster recovery and chaos engineering
lessons.summary: Set RPO and RTO targets, choose between backup-restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active, and prove it all works with drills and chaos experiments.

lessons.title: Observability with logs, metrics and traces
lessons.summary: Use structured logs, metrics and distributed traces together, apply the RED and USE methods, and instrument with OpenTelemetry.

lessons.title: SLIs, SLOs, SLAs and error budgets
lessons.summary: Choose SLIs that reflect user experience, set SLOs, turn them into error budgets, and alert with multi-window burn rates the way Google SRE does.

lessons.title: Safe deployments and zero-downtime migrations
lessons.summary: Compare rolling, blue-green and canary releases, decouple deploy from release with feature flags, and change database schemas without downtime using expand and contract.

lessons.title: Security in system design
lessons.summary: Encrypt in transit and at rest, manage keys with KMS and envelope encryption, enforce least privilege and zero trust, handle secrets properly, and design for OWASP risks and DDoS.

modules.title: Case Studies I
modules.summary: Full interview-style walkthroughs: a method for design interviews, then URL shortener, rate limiter, chat, news feed, notifications and typeahead.

lessons.title: A framework for system design interviews
lessons.summary: A repeatable seven-step method for a 45-minute design interview, how to spend the time, what interviewers actually score, and the mistakes that sink candidates.

lessons.title: Design a URL shortener
lessons.summary: Design a TinyURL/Bitly-style service, focusing on short-code generation (hashing, counters, Snowflake), 301 vs 302 redirects, caching and click analytics.

lessons.title: Design a distributed rate limiter
lessons.summary: Build a rate limiting service for a large API fleet, choosing between token bucket and sliding windows, keeping counters atomic in Redis, and deciding what happens when the limiter itself fails.

lessons.title: Design typeahead autocomplete
lessons.summary: Design search-box autocomplete that returns the top suggestions for every keystroke in tens of milliseconds, using tries with precomputed top-k, an offline aggregation pipeline and aggressive edge caching.

lessons.title: Design a notification system
lessons.summary: Design a multi-channel notification platform (push, SMS, email, in-app) with templating, user preferences, priority queues, deduplication, retries and provider failover.

lessons.title: Design a news feed like Twitter/X
lessons.summary: Design a home timeline for hundreds of millions of users, weighing fan-out on write against fan-out on read, solving the celebrity problem with a hybrid, caching timelines in Redis and adding ML ranking.

lessons.title: Design a chat system like WhatsApp
lessons.summary: Design 1:1 and group messaging for hundreds of millions of users, covering WebSocket gateways, message routing, delivery and read receipts, offline delivery, per-conversation ordering and presence.

modules.title: Case Studies II
modules.summary: Full interview-style walkthroughs of eight harder systems: video streaming, ride-sharing, a Dynamo-style key-value store, a web crawler, payments, collaborative editing, ticket booking and a distributed job scheduler.

lessons.title: Video streaming (YouTube / Netflix)
lessons.summary: Design a video platform end to end, covering resumable upload, a chunked transcoding pipeline, adaptive bitrate with HLS/DASH, and a CDN strategy like Netflix Open Connect.

lessons.title: Ride-sharing (Uber / Lyft)
lessons.summary: Design a ride-hailing backend, covering high-rate driver location ingestion, geospatial indexing with geohash, quadtrees, S2 and H3, rider-driver matching, and surge pricing.

lessons.title: Web crawler
lessons.summary: Design a distributed crawler for billions of pages, covering the URL frontier, politeness and robots.txt, dedup with Bloom filters and SimHash, spider traps, and partitioning by host.

lessons.title: Ticket booking (Ticketmaster)
lessons.summary: Design a ticketing platform that never double-sells a seat, covering seat holds with expiry, the concurrency control that makes booking safe, and virtual waiting rooms for flash-sale traffic.

lessons.title: Distributed job scheduler (cron at scale)
lessons.summary: Design a multi-tenant scheduler that fires millions of one-off and cron jobs on time, covering delayed queues, leader election with fencing, sharding, at-least-once execution and the cron edge cases that bite.

lessons.title: Payment system
lessons.summary: Design a payments platform that prevents duplicate postings and detects unresolved money movements, covering payment state machines, idempotency keys, a double-entry ledger, PSP integration with webhooks, and daily reconciliation.

lessons.title: Collaborative editor (Google Docs)
lessons.summary: Design real-time co-editing, covering operational transformation versus CRDTs, a per-document session server, presence and cursors, offline edits, and storing revisions as an op log plus snapshots.

lessons.title: Distributed key-value store (Dynamo / Cassandra)
lessons.summary: Design a leaderless, availability-oriented key-value store, covering consistent hashing with virtual nodes, quorum replication, sloppy quorums and hinted handoff, vector clocks versus last-write-wins, gossip, Merkle-tree repair and LSM compaction.

subjects.title: Data Structures & Algorithms
subjects.description: Complexity, core data structures, sorting, graphs, dynamic programming and the problem-solving patterns behind coding interviews.

modules.title: Complexity Analysis
modules.summary: How to measure and reason about the cost of algorithms: growth rates, Big-O/Omega/Theta, analysing code, space, amortised analysis, recurrences and the Master Theorem, and what complexity means on real hardware.

lessons.title: Algorithms and why efficiency matters
lessons.summary: What an algorithm is, how to count the work it does, and why the growth rate of that count matters far more than the speed of your computer.

lessons.title: Big-O, Big-Omega and Big-Theta
lessons.summary: The formal definitions behind asymptotic notation, how to prove a bound, why constants and lower-order terms vanish, and the ladder of common complexity classes from O(1) to O(n!).

lessons.title: Analysing code
lessons.summary: How to read the complexity off real code, including dependent and logarithmic loops, recursion, hidden library costs, and best, average and worst case.

lessons.title: Space complexity
lessons.summary: Measuring memory as well as time, auxiliary versus total space, the hidden cost of the recursion stack, in-place algorithms and time-space trade-offs.

lessons.title: Amortised analysis
lessons.summary: Why appending to a dynamic array is O(1) even though some appends copy everything, and the aggregate, accounting and potential methods for proving it.

lessons.title: Recurrences and the Master Theorem
lessons.summary: Turning recursive code into recurrences, solving them with recursion trees, the three cases of the Master Theorem, where it fails, and the Akra–Bazzi generalisation for uneven splits.

lessons.title: Complexity in practice
lessons.summary: What Big-O leaves out and when it matters, from constant factors and CPU caches to what input sizes are feasible in a second, adversarial inputs, galactic algorithms and how to choose between algorithms.

modules.title: Arrays, Lists, Stacks & Queues
modules.summary: The linear data structures everything else is built on: how arrays sit in memory, mutable and immutable string representations, linked lists and their pointer tricks, stacks, queues, deques and a first look at priority queues.

lessons.title: Arrays and memory
lessons.summary: Why arrays give O(1) indexing, how contiguous memory and CPU caches make them fast, and how dynamic arrays like Python's list, Java's ArrayList and C++'s vector grow.

lessons.title: Strings
lessons.summary: Strings as arrays of characters, why most languages make them immutable, what encodings do to length and indexing, why concatenating in a loop is quadratic, and the real cost of common string operations.

lessons.title: Linked lists
lessons.summary: Singly, doubly and circular linked lists, how sentinel nodes remove edge cases, the real costs of insertion and deletion, and the specific situations where linked lists beat arrays.

lessons.title: Classic linked-list techniques
lessons.summary: The handful of pointer patterns behind almost every linked-list problem — in-place reversal, fast and slow pointers (Floyd's cycle detection, finding the middle), merging sorted lists and dummy heads — with traces and proofs.

lessons.title: Stacks
lessons.summary: The last-in, first-out stack, how to implement it on an array or a linked list, the call stack that runs your programs, and the classic stack algorithms — balanced brackets, expression evaluation and the monotonic stack.

lessons.title: Queues and deques
lessons.summary: First-in, first-out queues and why a plain array makes a bad one, circular buffers, double-ended queues, the queue at the heart of breadth-first search, monotonic deques, and a first look at priority queues.

modules.title: Hash Tables & Hashing
modules.summary: Hash maps and sets, hash functions, collision resolution, resizing and real implementations, the hashing patterns behind interview problems, and probabilistic structures like Bloom filters and HyperLogLog.

lessons.title: Hash maps and sets
lessons.summary: What a hash map and a hash set promise, why lookups are O(1) on average but O(n) in the worst case, and when to reach for one.

lessons.title: Hash functions
lessons.summary: What makes a good hash function, the division and multiplication methods, polynomial string hashing, universal hashing, and how hash flooding attacks forced languages to randomise their hashes.

lessons.title: Collision resolution
lessons.summary: Separate chaining versus open addressing, linear and quadratic probing, double hashing, tombstones for deletion, and how Robin Hood hashing and Swiss tables tame probe lengths.

lessons.title: Load factor and resizing
lessons.summary: Why tables grow at a fixed load factor, why doubling makes inserts amortised O(1), and how CPython's dict and Java's HashMap (with its Java 8 tree bins) actually work.

lessons.title: Hashing patterns for problems
lessons.summary: The hash map patterns behind a large share of coding problems: complement lookup (two-sum), frequency maps, grouping by a canonical key, prefix sums with a map, and sliding windows that track counts.

lessons.title: Probabilistic structures
lessons.summary: Bloom filters, Count-Min Sketch and HyperLogLog trade a small, controllable error for enormous memory savings; this lesson covers how they work, the false-positive maths, and where databases and Redis use them.

modules.title: Trees & Heaps
modules.summary: Binary trees, traversals, binary search trees, AVL and red-black balancing, heaps and priority queues, tries, and the classic tree problems that come up in interviews and real systems.

lessons.title: Tree basics
lessons.summary: What a tree is, the vocabulary (root, leaf, height, depth), binary trees, how they are stored in memory, and the difference between full, complete, perfect and balanced.

lessons.title: Tree traversals
lessons.summary: Pre-order, in-order, post-order and level-order traversal, recursive and iterative versions, what each is good for, and Morris traversal for O(1) extra space.

lessons.title: Binary search trees
lessons.summary: The BST ordering rule, search and insert, the three cases of delete, finding successors, validating a BST correctly, and why sorted input turns a BST into a linked list.

lessons.title: Balanced search trees
lessons.summary: Rotations, AVL trees and red-black trees, the invariants that guarantee O(log n) height, how they compare, and where they run in practice (Java TreeMap, C++ std::map, the Linux scheduler).

lessons.title: Heaps and priority queues
lessons.summary: The binary heap's array layout, sift up and sift down, why heapify is O(n), Python's heapq, and the top-k and k-way merge patterns.

lessons.title: Tries
lessons.summary: Prefix trees for strings, with insert, search and prefix queries in time proportional to the key length, the memory costs, compressed tries and radix trees, and how autocomplete is built on them.

lessons.title: Common tree problems
lessons.summary: The recurring patterns behind tree interview problems and real code, worked through lowest common ancestor, diameter, path sums, serialisation and rebuilding a tree from its traversals.

modules.title: Sorting & Searching
modules.summary: From bubble sort to Timsort and pdqsort: how the classic sorts work, the worst-case n log n lower bound for general comparison sorting, when linear-time sorts apply, binary search without off-by-one bugs, and selecting the k-th smallest.

lessons.title: Simple sorts and what they teach
lessons.summary: Bubble, selection and insertion sort, and the vocabulary they introduce: stability, in-place, adaptive behaviour and inversions.

lessons.title: Merge sort
lessons.summary: Divide and conquer, the linear-time merge, why merge sort is stable, the recursion-tree proof of O(n log n), and how external merge sort handles data bigger than memory.

lessons.title: Quicksort
lessons.summary: Lomuto and Hoare partitioning, pivot choice, the O(n²) worst case and how randomisation, 3-way partitioning and introsort defend against it.

lessons.title: Heapsort and the comparison-sort lower bound
lessons.summary: How heapsort gets O(n log n) worst case in O(1) space, why it is slower than quicksort in practice, and the decision-tree proof that no comparison sort can beat Ω(n log n).

lessons.title: Linear-time sorts
lessons.summary: Counting sort, radix sort and bucket sort escape the n log n bound by using keys as indices; here is how they work, what they really cost, and when they apply.

lessons.title: Real-world sorting
lessons.summary: What your language's sort actually does (Timsort, pdqsort, introsort, dual-pivot quicksort), how runs and galloping exploit real data, and how comparators, keys and stability go wrong in production.

lessons.title: Binary search done right
lessons.summary: Writing binary search from an invariant so it is correct first time, lower and upper bound, the classic overflow and infinite-loop bugs, rotated arrays and binary search on the answer.

lessons.title: Selection: quickselect, median of medians and heaps
lessons.summary: Finding the k-th smallest element without sorting, in expected O(n) with quickselect, worst-case O(n) with median of medians, and O(n log(k + 1)) with a heap for top-k and streams.

modules.title: Graphs
modules.summary: Representations, BFS and DFS, topological sort and SCCs, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees with Union-Find, and network flow, matching, bridges and articulation points.

lessons.title: Graph fundamentals and representations
lessons.summary: Vertices, edges, direction and weight; adjacency lists, matrices and edge lists; and the implicit graphs hiding in grids and puzzles.

lessons.title: BFS and DFS
lessons.summary: The two fundamental traversals, how visited sets keep them linear, and how they give you components, flood fill and unweighted shortest paths.

lessons.title: Cycles, topological sort and SCCs
lessons.summary: Using DFS structure to detect cycles, order dependencies with Kahn's algorithm or DFS finish times, find strongly connected components with Tarjan or Kosaraju, and test bipartiteness.

lessons.title: Shortest paths with weights
lessons.summary: Dijkstra with a binary heap and why negative edges break it, Bellman–Ford and negative cycles, 0-1 BFS, and A* with admissible heuristics.

lessons.title: All-pairs shortest paths
lessons.summary: Floyd–Warshall as dynamic programming over intermediate vertices, transitive closure with bitsets, and when running Dijkstra (or Johnson's algorithm) n times is the better choice.

lessons.title: Minimum spanning trees and Union-Find
lessons.summary: The cut property, Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, and the Union-Find structure whose path compression and union by rank make operations effectively constant time.

lessons.title: Flow, matching, bridges and articulation points
lessons.summary: Maximum flow with Ford–Fulkerson and Edmonds–Karp, the max-flow min-cut theorem, bipartite matching as flow, and finding single points of failure with DFS low-link values.

modules.title: Recursion, Backtracking & Greedy
modules.summary: Thinking recursively, divide and conquer, backtracking search with pruning and constraint propagation, greedy algorithms and how to prove them, and how to spot when greedy fails.

lessons.title: Thinking recursively
lessons.summary: Base cases, the recursive leap of faith, what the call stack really does, tail recursion (and why Python won't optimise it), and how to turn recursion into a loop.

lessons.title: Divide and conquer
lessons.summary: Split a problem into independent halves, solve them recursively and combine the answers; with the master theorem, merge sort, fast exponentiation, Karatsuba multiplication and the closest pair of points.

lessons.title: Backtracking
lessons.summary: The choose, explore, unchoose template for searching every possibility, applied to subsets, permutations and combinations, and how pruning cuts the search down.

lessons.title: Backtracking problems in depth
lessons.summary: N-Queens, Sudoku and word search worked through properly, then the techniques real solvers use to tame exponential search: smart variable ordering, forward checking and constraint propagation.

lessons.title: Greedy algorithms
lessons.summary: Make the locally best choice and never look back; how to prove that works with the greedy choice property and exchange arguments, applied to interval scheduling, meeting rooms and Huffman coding.

lessons.title: When greedy fails
lessons.summary: Coin systems where greedy gives the wrong change, why fractional knapsack is greedy but 0/1 knapsack isn't, and a practical method for telling a greedy problem from a dynamic programming one.

modules.title: Dynamic Programming
modules.summary: Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, a repeatable method for designing recurrences, and the classic families: 1-D, grids and strings, knapsack, interval, tree, bitmask, digit and DAG DP.

lessons.title: What dynamic programming is
lessons.summary: Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, how Fibonacci goes from exponential to linear, and the difference between memoisation and tabulation.

lessons.title: A method for solving DP problems
lessons.summary: A five-step recipe (state, recurrence, base cases, evaluation order, reconstruction) applied to word break and a stock-trading state machine.

lessons.title: 1-D DP
lessons.summary: Climbing stairs, house robber, coin change (minimum coins and number of ways) and longest increasing subsequence in both O(n²) and O(n log n).

lessons.title: 2-D DP on grids and strings
lessons.summary: Unique paths, edit distance and longest common subsequence as tables, how to read and reconstruct them, and how to cut memory to one or two rows.

lessons.title: The knapsack family
lessons.summary: 0/1 and unbounded knapsack, subset sum and partition, why the loop direction matters, and why O(n·W) is pseudo-polynomial rather than polynomial.

lessons.title: Interval and tree DP
lessons.summary: DP over ranges (matrix chain multiplication, burst balloons, palindromes), evaluated by interval length, and DP over trees (maximum independent set), evaluated bottom-up from the leaves.

lessons.title: Advanced DP and spotting DP problems
lessons.summary: Bitmask DP and Held–Karp for the travelling salesman, digit DP for counting numbers with digit constraints, DP over DAGs as the unifying view, and how to recognise a DP problem from its constraints.

modules.title: Problem-Solving Patterns
modules.summary: How to recognise which technique a coding-interview problem needs: two pointers, sliding windows, prefix sums, monotonic stacks, intervals, heaps and bit tricks, each with a template and classic problems worked through.

lessons.title: How to approach a coding problem
lessons.summary: A repeatable five-step method (clarify, examples, brute force, optimise, test), how input sizes tell you the target complexity, and how to talk through it in an interview.

lessons.title: Two pointers
lessons.summary: Using two indices that move through an array to replace a nested loop with a single pass, in three flavours (opposite ends, same direction and partitioning), with pair sum, container with most water, remove duplicates and the Dutch flag.

lessons.title: Sliding window
lessons.summary: Maintaining a contiguous window incrementally instead of recomputing it, with fixed and variable windows, longest substring without repeats, minimum window substring and the at-most-k counting trick.

lessons.title: Prefix sums and difference arrays
lessons.summary: Precomputing running totals to answer range sums in O(1), counting subarrays that sum to k with a hash map, applying range updates with difference arrays, and extending it all to 2-D grids.

lessons.title: Intervals
lessons.summary: Sorting intervals to merge and insert them, choosing the most non-overlapping ones greedily, and counting the rooms a schedule needs with a min-heap or a sweep line.

lessons.title: Monotonic stacks and queues
lessons.summary: Keeping a stack or deque in sorted order so each element is pushed and popped once, giving O(n) solutions to next greater element, largest rectangle in a histogram and sliding window maximum.

lessons.title: Top-K, k-way merge and two heaps
lessons.summary: Three heap patterns that recur in interviews and production systems, a size-k heap for the k largest, a heap of list heads to merge k sorted inputs, and a pair of heaps to track a running median.

lessons.title: Bit manipulation
lessons.summary: The handful of bit tricks that keep coming up, such as x & (x-1), x & -x and XOR cancellation, plus bitmasks for subsets and DP, counting set bits, and the traps of Python's unbounded integers.

modules.title: Advanced Structures & Algorithms
modules.summary: Composite designs like LRU and LFU caches, union-find, segment and Fenwick trees, string matching with KMP, Rabin–Karp and suffix arrays, randomised structures, sparse tables, and a tour of persistent structures and ropes.

lessons.title: Designing data structures
lessons.summary: How to combine a hash map with a linked list or an array to get O(1) operations, worked through LRU caches, LFU caches and a set with O(1) getRandom.

lessons.title: Union-Find in depth
lessons.summary: The disjoint-set forest, why path compression and union by rank or size make it almost O(1), and how it powers Kruskal's algorithm, connectivity and accounts merging.

lessons.title: Segment trees
lessons.summary: A binary tree of range summaries that answers range queries and applies updates in O(log n), plus lazy propagation for updating whole ranges at once.

lessons.title: Fenwick trees
lessons.summary: The binary indexed tree, a ten-line structure for prefix sums with updates in O(log n), how the lowbit trick drives it, and when to choose it over a segment tree.

lessons.title: String algorithms
lessons.summary: Linear-time pattern matching with KMP, rolling hashes with Rabin–Karp, the Z-function, and an introduction to suffix arrays and LCP arrays for many-query string problems.

lessons.title: Randomised structures and sampling
lessons.summary: How coin flips replace rebalancing in skip lists and treaps, and how reservoir sampling and the Fisher–Yates shuffle produce provably uniform random choices.

lessons.title: Sparse tables, persistence and ropes
lessons.summary: O(1) range-minimum queries with sparse tables, then a tour of persistent data structures built by path copying, and ropes for editing very long strings.

subjects.title: Operating Systems
subjects.description: Processes, threads, scheduling, concurrency, memory, file systems, I/O and virtualisation.

modules.title: OS Basics & Processes
modules.summary: What an operating system is for, how programs cross into the kernel, what a process really is, how processes are created, switched and reaped, and how they talk to each other.

lessons.title: What an operating system does
lessons.summary: The three jobs of an OS (abstraction, resource management, protection), the line between kernel and user space, and how monolithic, micro- and hybrid kernels draw it differently.

lessons.title: System calls and CPU modes
lessons.summary: User and kernel mode, the difference between traps, exceptions and interrupts, what actually happens on a Linux x86-64 syscall, what one costs, and how the vDSO avoids the cost entirely.

lessons.title: The process abstraction
lessons.summary: What a process is, how its virtual address space is laid out (text, data, BSS, heap, mmap, stack), what the kernel keeps in the process control block, and the states a process moves through.

lessons.title: Creating processes: fork, exec and wait
lessons.summary: How Unix creates processes with fork and exec, how copy-on-write makes fork cheap, how parents collect exit codes with wait, and what zombies, orphans and PID 1 are really about.

lessons.title: Context switching
lessons.summary: How the kernel pauses one task and resumes another, exactly what state is saved, what a switch costs directly and through caches and the TLB, and a first look at user versus kernel threads.

lessons.title: Inter-process communication
lessons.summary: How isolated processes talk to each other on Linux, using pipes, signals, shared memory, message queues and sockets, and how to choose between them.

modules.title: Threads & Scheduling
modules.summary: What threads are and how to use them, then how the OS decides who runs: classic algorithms, priorities and MLFQ, Linux's CFS and EEVDF, real-time classes, and scheduling across many cores and inside containers.

lessons.title: Threads
lessons.summary: Why threads exist, what they share and what they keep private, kernel versus user threads, the 1:1, N:1 and M:N models, and how goroutines fit in.

lessons.title: Thread APIs in practice
lessons.summary: Creating, joining and detaching POSIX threads in C, the bugs everyone writes first, thread pools and how to size them, and what Python's GIL does and does not protect you from.

lessons.title: CPU scheduling basics
lessons.summary: What a scheduler is trying to optimise, CPU-bound versus I/O-bound work, preemption, and FCFS, SJF, SRTF and round robin worked through with Gantt charts.

lessons.title: Priorities, MLFQ and starvation
lessons.summary: Priority scheduling and its failure modes, the multilevel feedback queue that learns which jobs are interactive, aging, and priority inversion from Mars Pathfinder to priority inheritance.

lessons.title: Linux scheduling - CFS, EEVDF and real-time classes
lessons.summary: How Linux actually picks the next thread - scheduling classes, CFS's virtual runtime and weights, nice values, the EEVDF scheduler that replaced CFS in 6.6, and the SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR and SCHED_DEADLINE real-time policies.

lessons.title: Multicore scheduling, affinity, NUMA and containers
lessons.summary: Scheduling across many CPUs - per-CPU run queues, load balancing and cache affinity, pinning with sched_setaffinity and cpusets, NUMA locality, and why CPU limits in containers cause throttling and tail latency.

modules.title: Concurrency & Synchronisation
modules.summary: Shared-memory coordination: locks, futexes, semaphores, condition variables, classic synchronisation problems, atomics, memory ordering, lock-free algorithms and RCU.

lessons.title: Race conditions and critical sections
lessons.summary: Why counter++ is not atomic, how interleavings lose updates, the difference between a data race and a race condition, and what any solution to the critical-section problem must guarantee.

lessons.title: Locks, spinlocks and futexes
lessons.summary: How mutexes and spinlocks are built from test-and-set and compare-and-swap, why Linux mutexes sit on futexes, and how contention and lock granularity decide whether your threads actually run in parallel.

lessons.title: Semaphores, condition variables and monitors
lessons.summary: Counting and binary semaphores, how condition variables let threads sleep until a condition holds, why you always re-check the condition in a while loop, and how monitors package it all up.

lessons.title: Classic synchronisation problems
lessons.summary: The bounded buffer, readers–writers, dining philosophers and sleeping barber problems, solved with semaphores and condition variables, and the real systems each one models.

lessons.title: Atomics and memory ordering
lessons.summary: Atomic operations, how compilers and CPUs reorder memory accesses, memory barriers, acquire/release and sequential consistency in C11, happens-before, and why double-checked locking was broken for years.

lessons.title: Lock-free structures, RCU and read-write locks
lessons.summary: Progress guarantees, CAS retry loops and the Treiber stack, the ABA problem and safe memory reclamation, and the read-mostly toolkit of read-write locks, seqlocks and RCU.

modules.title: Deadlock & Liveness
modules.summary: Why threads and transactions get stuck forever, how to prevent, avoid, detect and recover from deadlock, the subtler liveness failures (livelock, starvation, priority inversion) and the tools that find them.

lessons.title: What deadlock is
lessons.summary: The four Coffman conditions, resource-allocation graphs, and the everyday ways code and databases end up stuck forever.

lessons.title: Deadlock prevention
lessons.summary: Make deadlock structurally impossible by breaking one Coffman condition, with lock ordering, try-lock and back-off, and lock hierarchies.

lessons.title: Avoidance and the Banker's algorithm
lessons.summary: Safe and unsafe states, and Dijkstra's Banker's algorithm worked through with real matrices, plus the practical assumptions that limit its use.

lessons.title: Detection and recovery
lessons.summary: Letting deadlocks happen, finding them with wait-for graphs and the multi-instance detection algorithm, breaking them by choosing a victim, and how PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server do it.

lessons.title: Livelock, starvation and priority inversion
lessons.summary: The liveness failures that aren't deadlock, from polite threads that never stop retrying to unfair locks and high-priority work stuck behind low-priority work, and the fixes for each.

lessons.title: Debugging deadlocks and designing them out
lessons.summary: Diagnosing a hung process with thread dumps, gdb and database lock views, catching lock-order bugs before they bite with lockdep and ThreadSanitizer, and the design rules that keep deadlock out of a codebase.

modules.title: Memory Management
modules.summary: Virtual memory from first principles: address spaces, paging and x86-64 page tables, the TLB, page faults and copy-on-write, page replacement, malloc and kernel allocators, and debugging memory on real Linux systems and containers.

lessons.title: Address spaces and why virtual memory exists
lessons.summary: Physical versus virtual addresses, what an address space gives each process, and the historical base-and-bounds and segmentation schemes that paging replaced.

lessons.title: Paging and page tables
lessons.summary: Pages and frames, what a page table entry holds, translating an address bit by bit, and why x86-64 uses a 4- or 5-level tree of tables.

lessons.title: The TLB and huge pages
lessons.summary: How the translation lookaside buffer makes paging fast, effective access time calculations, TLB reach, ASIDs and PCIDs across context switches, shootdowns, and when huge pages help or hurt.

lessons.title: Page faults, copy-on-write, mmap and swap
lessons.summary: What happens when a page table entry says "not here", how Linux uses that one exception to build demand paging, copy-on-write fork, memory-mapped files and swap, and what each kind of fault costs.

lessons.title: Page replacement and thrashing
lessons.summary: When RAM is full, which page goes? FIFO, the optimal algorithm, LRU and the clock approximation traced by hand, Belady's anomaly, how Linux actually reclaims memory, and why too little memory makes a machine thrash.

lessons.title: Memory allocators, from malloc to slab
lessons.summary: How user-space malloc carves pages into objects (glibc's chunks, bins, tcache and arenas), why freed memory often doesn't return to the OS, and how the kernel allocates memory with the buddy system and the slab allocator, plus what jemalloc, tcmalloc and mimalloc do differently.

lessons.title: Overcommit, OOM, RSS and cgroups in production
lessons.summary: How overcommit changes allocation failure on Linux, how the OOM killer picks a victim, what VSZ, RSS, PSS and USS really measure, how cgroup v2 and Kubernetes limit memory, and the tools for hunting leaks.

modules.title: File Systems & Storage
modules.summary: Files and descriptors, inodes and on-disk layout, crash consistency and fsync, the page cache, HDDs, SSDs and RAID, and the modern and distributed file systems built on top.

lessons.title: The file abstraction
lessons.summary: Files, directories and paths, file descriptors and the open/read/write/close calls, the three tables behind every descriptor, the VFS layer and what "everything is a file" really means on Linux.

lessons.title: On-disk structures
lessons.summary: How a file system lays files out on a block device, from superblock, bitmaps and inodes to directory entries, hard and symbolic links, and the allocation strategies (contiguous, FAT, indexed and extents) that decide where the bytes go.

lessons.title: Crash consistency, journaling and fsync
lessons.summary: Why a power cut mid-update can corrupt a file system, how fsck, journaling (ext4's ordered mode) and copy-on-write (ZFS, Btrfs) defend against it, and the fsync pitfalls behind PostgreSQL's 2018 "fsyncgate".

lessons.title: The page cache and buffering
lessons.summary: How Linux caches file data in RAM, read-ahead and write-back, dirty pages and the knobs that control them, O_DIRECT, mmap versus read, and zero-copy with sendfile.

lessons.title: HDDs, SSDs, NVMe and RAID
lessons.summary: How spinning disks and flash actually store data, what the flash translation layer hides, why NVMe replaced SATA, and the capacity, performance and failure maths of RAID.

lessons.title: Real file systems, from ext4 to HDFS
lessons.summary: How ext4, XFS, Btrfs and ZFS differ in practice, the log-structured idea behind LFS and F2FS, and how NFS, GFS and HDFS stretch a file system across a network.

modules.title: I/O & Event-Driven Servers
modules.summary: How the CPU talks to devices, the five I/O models, select/poll/epoll/kqueue, io_uring, how event-loop servers like Node.js, nginx and Redis are built, and the path a packet takes through the Linux networking stack.

lessons.title: How I/O works
lessons.summary: Device controllers and registers, polling versus interrupts, DMA, what a device driver does, and how Linux splits interrupt handling into top and bottom halves.

lessons.title: The five I/O models
lessons.summary: Blocking, non-blocking, multiplexed, signal-driven and asynchronous I/O as Stevens classified them, readiness versus completion, and what "async" actually means.

lessons.title: select, poll and epoll
lessons.summary: How select, poll, epoll and kqueue work inside, why their costs differ, level- versus edge-triggered notification, and how they solved the C10K problem.

lessons.title: io_uring
lessons.summary: Linux's completion-based I/O interface, how its shared submission and completion rings work, how it can reduce per-operation overhead, and why Google, Docker and others restrict it.

lessons.title: Event loops (libuv, nginx, Redis)
lessons.summary: How an event loop turns epoll or kqueue into a server, the reactor and proactor patterns, timers, libuv's phases and thread pool, nginx's worker model, Redis's single-threaded design, and the cardinal rule of never blocking the loop.

lessons.title: The kernel network stack, NAPI, RSS, DPDK, eBPF/XDP
lessons.summary: The path a packet takes from the NIC to your recv() and back, how NAPI, GRO and RSS keep up with millions of packets a second, and when to bypass the kernel with DPDK or program it with eBPF and XDP.

modules.title: Virtualisation & Containers
modules.summary: Hypervisors and hardware support for guest operating systems, Linux container primitives such as namespaces and cgroups, image layers, isolation and security, and how Kubernetes uses these components.

lessons.title: Virtualisation basics
lessons.summary: Why we run operating systems inside other operating systems, type 1 and type 2 hypervisors, trap-and-emulate, the Popek–Goldberg rules, and the binary translation and paravirtualisation tricks x86 needed.

lessons.title: Hardware-assisted virtualisation
lessons.summary: How VT-x and AMD-V add a guest mode to the CPU, how nested page tables avoid much shadow-paging synchronisation work, how virtio and SR-IOV make I/O fast, and how a running VM is live-migrated between hosts.

lessons.title: Containers from first principles
lessons.summary: There is no 'container' in the Linux kernel. Here is what there is instead, namespaces, cgroups v2, pivot_root and overlay file systems, and how they combine into one.

lessons.title: Container runtimes and images
lessons.summary: What is actually inside an OCI image, how Docker, containerd and runc divide the work of running one, and how layer caching makes builds fast or painfully slow.

lessons.title: Isolating containers
lessons.summary: How capabilities, seccomp, LSMs and user namespaces shrink what a container can do to a shared kernel, and when to reach for gVisor or a Firecracker microVM instead.

lessons.title: Kubernetes through the OS lens
lessons.summary: What a pod really is on a Linux node, how requests and limits become cgroup files, why CPU limits throttle and memory limits kill, and how securityContext and RuntimeClass map onto the isolation tools from earlier lessons.

subjects.title: Computer Networks
subjects.description: How data actually moves: the layers, IP and routing, TCP in depth, protocols and network security.

modules.title: Network Foundations & the Link Layer
modules.summary: Layered models and encapsulation, network delays, signals on copper, fibre and radio, Ethernet, switching, ARP and spanning tree, error detection and link-layer retransmission where supported.

lessons.title: Layered models and encapsulation
lessons.summary: OSI versus TCP/IP, how each layer wraps the one above in its own header, a byte-by-byte packet walk-through, and the places where the neat layering breaks down.

lessons.title: Bandwidth, latency and throughput
lessons.summary: The four components of delay and how to calculate each, why queues explode near full load, the bandwidth-delay product, and why throughput and goodput are lower than the link speed.

lessons.title: The physical layer in brief
lessons.summary: How bits become signals, why line codes exist, the Nyquist and Shannon limits, and how copper, fibre and radio differ, including why signals in fibre travel at about two-thirds of the speed of light.

lessons.title: Ethernet and the link layer
lessons.summary: The Ethernet frame field by field, MAC addresses, how CSMA/CD shared a cable and why it no longer matters, how switches learn where hosts are, VLANs and the 1500-byte MTU.

lessons.title: ARP, spoofing and spanning tree
lessons.summary: How a host finds the MAC address for an IP address, why ARP is trivially spoofable and how networks defend against it, and how spanning tree stops switch loops from melting a LAN.

lessons.title: Error detection and sliding-window ARQ
lessons.summary: Parity, the Internet checksum and CRCs worked by hand, what each can and can't catch, and the maths of stop-and-wait, Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat, including why sequence numbers limit the window.

modules.title: IP, Addressing & Routing
modules.summary: The network layer in depth: the IPv4 header, ICMP and traceroute, subnetting and CIDR, NAT and IPv6, how routers forward and build their tables, RIP and OSPF, BGP and its incidents, and DHCP.

lessons.title: IPv4, fragmentation and ICMP
lessons.summary: The IPv4 header field by field, what TTL is really for, how fragmentation and Path MTU Discovery work, and how ping and traceroute use ICMP.

lessons.title: Addressing and subnetting
lessons.summary: How IPv4 addresses split into network and host parts, CIDR and subnet masks, calculating network, broadcast and host ranges by hand, private ranges, and route aggregation.

lessons.title: NAT and IPv6
lessons.summary: How NAT and port translation stretch IPv4, why they break end-to-end connectivity, how STUN, TURN and ICE get around them, and how IPv6 addressing, SLAAC and dual stack work.

lessons.title: Forwarding and longest-prefix match
lessons.summary: What a router actually does with each packet, how the routing table is built and searched with longest-prefix match, what changes at every hop, and how tries and hardware tables accelerate lookup.

lessons.title: RIP vs OSPF
lessons.summary: How routers inside one network learn their tables automatically, comparing distance-vector RIP and its count-to-infinity problem with link-state OSPF, Dijkstra, costs, areas and designated routers.

lessons.title: BGP, hijacks and RPKI
lessons.summary: How independent networks glue the Internet together with BGP, how routes are chosen by policy rather than distance, how hijacks and leaks happen, and what RPKI does and doesn't fix.

lessons.title: DHCP and joining a network
lessons.summary: How a device with no address gets one through DHCP's four-message exchange, how leases, relays and snooping work, and a step-by-step trace of everything that happens from plugging in to the first packet reaching a remote server.

modules.title: Transport Layer: TCP & UDP in Depth
modules.summary: UDP and ports, the TCP handshake and state machine, sequence numbers and retransmission, flow and congestion control (Reno, CUBIC, BBR), real-world TCP performance, and the Berkeley sockets API.

lessons.title: UDP, ports and multiplexing
lessons.summary: What the transport layer adds on top of IP, the 8-byte UDP header, how ports and 5-tuples route data to the right socket, and when UDP beats TCP (DNS, games, QUIC).

lessons.title: TCP connection management
lessons.summary: The three-way handshake with real sequence numbers, SYN floods and SYN cookies, the four-way close, why TIME_WAIT lasts 2×MSL, the TCP state machine and when connections are reset.

lessons.title: Sequence numbers, ACKs and retransmission
lessons.summary: How TCP turns a lossy packet network into a reliable byte stream: cumulative ACKs, SACK, the RTO calculation from RFC 6298, fast retransmit on duplicate ACKs, and modern loss detection with RACK-TLP.

lessons.title: Flow control, window scaling, Nagle and delayed ACK
lessons.summary: How the receive window stops a fast sender drowning a slow receiver, why a 64 KB window caps throughput on long paths, window scaling and buffer autotuning, zero windows, and how Nagle and delayed ACKs can interact to delay small messages.

lessons.title: Congestion control: Reno, CUBIC and BBR
lessons.summary: Why TCP must slow down for the network's sake, slow start and AIMD traced RTT by RTT, Reno's fast recovery, CUBIC's cubic growth curve, BBR's model-based pacing, ECN, and the fairness trade-offs between them.

lessons.title: TCP performance in the real world
lessons.summary: Where the time goes in a TCP transfer, the Mathis formula linking loss to throughput, bufferbloat and active queue management, head-of-line blocking, why TCP is hard to change, and how QUIC rebuilds the transport in user space.

lessons.title: The sockets API and a Python server
lessons.summary: How Berkeley socket calls map onto TCP's states and queues, why TCP has no message boundaries and how to frame messages, partial sends and EOF, SO_REUSEADDR, and building a correct Python server with threads and with an event loop.

modules.title: Application-Layer Protocols
modules.summary: The bytes behind the protocols you use every day: HTTP/1.1 framing and cookies, HTTP/2 frames and HPACK, QUIC packets, the DNS wire format and DNSSEC, email and its authentication, NTP, SSH and gRPC, and peer-to-peer systems from BitTorrent to WebRTC.

lessons.title: HTTP/1.1 on the wire
lessons.summary: The exact bytes of an HTTP/1.1 exchange, how a receiver finds the end of a body, chunked transfer encoding, request smuggling, and the cookie attributes covered here and their security limits.

lessons.title: HTTP/2 frames, HPACK and QUIC packets
lessons.summary: The 9-byte HTTP/2 frame header, streams and flow control, how HPACK turns headers into single bytes, then QUIC's packet formats, variable-length integers, packet numbers and connection migration.

lessons.title: DNS on the wire, DNSSEC and encrypted DNS
lessons.summary: The DNS message format byte by byte, name compression, EDNS and truncation, how cache poisoning works and is defended, DNSSEC's chain of signatures, and what DoT and DoH do and do not hide.

lessons.title: Email: SMTP, IMAP, SPF, DKIM and DMARC
lessons.summary: How a message travels from submission to mailbox, a real SMTP session line by line, envelope versus header, IMAP's model of mailboxes and UIDs, and how SPF, DKIM and DMARC combine to stop spoofing.

lessons.title: NTP, SSH, SFTP and gRPC on the wire
lessons.summary: How NTP computes clock offset from four timestamps and why asymmetry fools it, the three layers of SSH and its binary packet, why SFTP is not FTP, and the exact bytes of a gRPC call over HTTP/2.

lessons.title: Peer to peer: BitTorrent, Kademlia, WebRTC and RTP
lessons.summary: How BitTorrent splits, verifies and trades pieces, how Kademlia's XOR metric supports logarithmic lookup under its routing assumptions, how WebRTC gets two browsers talking through NATs with ICE, STUN and TURN, and how RTP carries real-time media.

modules.title: Network Security
modules.summary: How networks are attacked and defended: eavesdropping, spoofing, MITM and DDoS, firewalls and segmentation, TLS 1.3 in depth, VPNs and tunnels, Wi-Fi security, and detecting intruders with IDS, packet captures and flow logs.

lessons.title: Threats on the network
lessons.summary: Eavesdropping, spoofing, man-in-the-middle, replay and denial of service, including how amplification attacks multiply an attacker's bandwidth and how to calculate by how much.

lessons.title: Firewalls, segmentation and zero trust
lessons.summary: Stateless and stateful packet filters, how rule order and connection tracking work, cloud security groups versus network ACLs, why flat networks get breached, and what zero trust actually changes.

lessons.title: TLS 1.3, certificates, ECH and mTLS
lessons.summary: What happens in a TLS 1.3 handshake and why each message is there, how certificate chains are validated and revoked, what Encrypted Client Hello hides, and how mutual TLS authenticates both ends.

lessons.title: IPsec, WireGuard, tunnels and VXLAN
lessons.summary: How tunnels encapsulate one network inside another, what IPsec and WireGuard add on top, how anti-replay windows work, why every tunnel shrinks the MTU and by how much, and why VXLAN overlays need protecting.

lessons.title: Wi-Fi security: WEP, WPA2, KRACK, WPA3 and 802.1X
lessons.summary: Why WEP fell apart, how the WPA2 four-way handshake derives keys and how KRACK broke it, how WPA2-Personal permits offline guessing, what correctly implemented SAE changes, and how enterprise authentication separates unicast keys.

lessons.title: Detecting intrusions with IDS, packet captures and flow logs
lessons.summary: How IDS and IPS work and why the base-rate problem drowns analysts in false alarms, how to capture and read traffic with tcpdump and Wireshark, and how NetFlow, IPFIX and cloud flow logs let you investigate at scale when payloads are encrypted.

modules.title: Wireless, Mobile & Modern Networks
modules.summary: Wi-Fi and cellular radio, the leaf-spine fabrics inside data centres, software-defined networks and cloud VPCs, the tools and method for debugging a slow network, and the cables, exchanges and satellites that make up the physical Internet.

lessons.title: Wi-Fi and 802.11
lessons.summary: How Wi-Fi shares the air with CSMA/CA, why hidden terminals need RTS/CTS, how channels interfere, what Wi-Fi 4 to 7 changed, and why advertised aggregate PHY rates differ from application throughput.

lessons.title: 4G and 5G networks, and what they mean for apps
lessons.summary: How a phone's packets travel through the radio network and the mobile core, how the radio's power states affect latency and battery use, and how to write apps that behave well on cellular.

lessons.title: Data-centre networks: leaf-spine, ECMP and oversubscription
lessons.summary: Why many data centres use Clos fabrics, how ECMP spreads flows across equal paths, and how to calculate oversubscription, scale and the cost of a failed spine.

lessons.title: Software-defined networking, OpenFlow and cloud VPCs
lessons.summary: Separating the control plane from the data plane, how OpenFlow match-action tables work, how overlays like VXLAN virtualise the network, and how a cloud VPC's subnets, route tables, security groups and NACLs actually behave.

lessons.title: Debugging networks, tools and method
lessons.summary: A repeatable method for "the network is slow" or "it can't connect", and how to read ping, traceroute, mtr, dig, curl timings, ss and tcpdump, including MTU black holes and loss-limited throughput.

lessons.title: How the Internet is built, from cables to satellites
lessons.summary: Autonomous systems, transit and peering, Tier 1 networks and IXPs, the submarine cables that carry intercontinental traffic, last-mile technologies, and the latency physics of fibre, GEO and LEO satellites.

subjects.title: Computer Architecture
subjects.description: From bits and logic gates to pipelines, caches, multicore and GPUs.

modules.title: Data Representation
modules.summary: How a computer turns everything into bits: number bases, integers and two's complement, bitwise tricks, IEEE 754 floating point, Unicode text, and how data is laid out in memory and on the wire.

lessons.title: Number systems and bases
lessons.summary: Binary, hexadecimal and octal, how to convert between them by hand, and what bits, bytes and words really are.

lessons.title: Two's complement and overflow
lessons.summary: How negative integers are stored, why two's complement won, sign extension, and what happens (and what C allows the compiler to assume) when arithmetic overflows.

lessons.title: Bitwise operations
lessons.summary: AND, OR, XOR, NOT and shifts, the mask idioms built from them, the classic bit tricks, and the C and Python rules that trip people up.

lessons.title: IEEE 754 floating point
lessons.summary: How floats and doubles are encoded bit by bit, why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3, what infinities, NaNs and subnormals are for, and how to compute with floats safely.

lessons.title: Unicode, UTF-8 and UTF-16
lessons.summary: From ASCII to Unicode code points, how UTF-8 and UTF-16 turn them into bytes bit by bit, and why string length, mojibake and normalisation catch so many programs out.

lessons.title: Endianness, alignment and struct padding
lessons.summary: How multi-byte values are ordered in memory and on the wire, why CPUs want data aligned, and how C compilers pad structs, with the bugs and security holes each one causes.

modules.title: Digital Logic
modules.summary: From Boolean algebra to working hardware: logic gates and the CMOS transistors behind them, Karnaugh-map minimisation, adders and ALUs, latches, flip-flops and state machines, and how a datapath, SRAM, DRAM and Verilog fit together.

lessons.title: Boolean algebra
lessons.summary: The algebra of true and false that every circuit is built on, its laws, De Morgan's theorem, truth tables, and the canonical sum-of-products and product-of-sums forms.

lessons.title: Logic gates and CMOS
lessons.summary: The seven standard gates, why NAND and NOR are universal, and how CMOS transistors build a gate, which explains why inverting gates are cheapest and where a chip's power goes.

lessons.title: Karnaugh maps
lessons.summary: A visual method for minimising Boolean functions of up to four or so variables, with Gray-code layout, prime implicants, don't-cares, product-of-sums, and the glitches that minimal circuits can cause.

lessons.title: Combinational circuits, adders and the ALU
lessons.summary: Multiplexers and decoders, the half and full adder, why ripple-carry is slow and how carry-lookahead and prefix adders fix it, subtraction in two's complement, and how an ALU produces its result and N, Z, C, V flags.

lessons.title: Latches, flip-flops and state machines
lessons.summary: How feedback lets a circuit remember, the SR and D latches, edge-triggered flip-flops and their setup, hold and clock-to-Q timing, metastability, and how to design a finite-state machine from a state diagram to gates.

lessons.title: Datapath, SRAM vs DRAM, and a first look at Verilog
lessons.summary: How registers, an ALU and muxes combine into a processor datapath driven by control signals, how SRAM and DRAM cells store bits and why one is fast and the other dense, and how hardware is actually written today in Verilog.

modules.title: Instruction Sets & Assembly
modules.summary: What the hardware actually runs: the stored-program machine and fetch–decode–execute, RISC versus CISC encodings and addressing modes, reading x86-64 and ARM64 assembly, calling conventions and stack frames, how loops, switches, arrays and structs compile, and how code is linked, loaded and hardened with NX, ASLR and stack canaries.

lessons.title: The stored-program computer and fetch–decode–execute
lessons.summary: Why programs live in memory as numbers, what the program counter does, how the fetch–decode–execute loop works, and what an instruction set architecture actually promises.

lessons.title: RISC vs CISC, instruction encoding and addressing modes
lessons.summary: How instructions are packed into bits on ARM64 and x86-64, why one is fixed-length and the other is not, the addressing modes both offer, and why the RISC vs CISC war mostly ended in a truce.

lessons.title: Reading x86-64 and ARM64 assembly
lessons.summary: The registers, syntax, flags and compiler idioms you need to read real x86-64 and ARM64 output from a compiler, debugger or profiler.

lessons.title: Calling conventions and stack frames
lessons.summary: How call and return work on x86-64 and ARM64, where arguments and return values go, which registers survive a call, and how stack frames, alignment and frame pointers fit together.

lessons.title: Loops, jump tables, arrays and structs in assembly
lessons.summary: How compilers lower if/else, loops and switch statements to branches and jump tables, and how array indexing and struct field access become address arithmetic.

lessons.title: Compile, assemble, link and load, plus NX, ASLR and canaries
lessons.summary: How source code becomes a running process (object files, relocations, ELF, static and dynamic linking through the PLT and GOT, the loader) and how NX, ASLR and stack canaries harden the result.

modules.title: Pipelining & CPU Performance
modules.summary: Why one CPU beats another: the iron law of performance, the classic 5-stage pipeline, hazards and forwarding, branch prediction, superscalar out-of-order cores and Tomasulo's algorithm, and the power wall that pushed the industry to multicore.

lessons.title: The iron law, CPI and IPC
lessons.summary: Why clock speed alone says little about performance, and how instruction count, cycles per instruction and clock period multiply together to give run time.

lessons.title: The 5-stage pipeline
lessons.summary: How splitting instruction execution into five overlapping stages lets a CPU finish one instruction per cycle, what each stage does, and why the speedup is less than five.

lessons.title: Hazards and forwarding
lessons.summary: The structural, data and control hazards that stop a pipeline completing one instruction per cycle, and how forwarding, stalls, scheduling and early branch resolution deal with them.

lessons.title: Branch prediction
lessons.summary: How CPUs guess the direction and target of branches before they are executed, from 2-bit counters to gshare and TAGE, what a misprediction costs, and how to write code that predicts well.

lessons.title: Superscalar, out-of-order and Tomasulo
lessons.summary: How modern cores finish several instructions per cycle by issuing them out of order, using register renaming, reservation stations, Tomasulo's algorithm and a reorder buffer, and what still limits them.

lessons.title: The power wall and multicore
lessons.summary: Why power constraints slowed clock scaling, the physics of dynamic power and Dennard scaling, and how the industry turned to multicore, frequency scaling, heterogeneous cores and specialisation.

modules.title: Caches & the Memory Hierarchy
modules.summary: Why memory is a hierarchy, how CPU caches are organised and addressed, write policies and AMAT maths, writing cache-friendly code, coherence and false sharing on multicore, and how DRAM, NUMA and prefetching shape real performance.

lessons.title: Locality and the memory hierarchy
lessons.summary: The latency, capacity and cost trade-offs behind memory hierarchies, and how temporal and spatial locality help caches.

lessons.title: Cache organisation and address breakdown
lessons.summary: How a cache decides where a line can live, splitting an address into tag, index and offset, direct-mapped vs set-associative vs fully associative, the three Cs of misses, and replacement policies.

lessons.title: Write policies and AMAT
lessons.summary: What happens on a store (write-through vs write-back, write-allocate vs no-write-allocate), how inclusion works between levels, and how to calculate average memory access time and stall CPI in an explicit blocking-cache model.

lessons.title: Writing cache-friendly code
lessons.summary: Loop order and row-major layout, counting misses per iteration, loop blocking (tiling) for matrix multiply, power-of-two stride traps, and structure-of-arrays versus array-of-structs.

lessons.title: Cache coherence (MESI) and false sharing
lessons.summary: How multicore CPUs keep private caches in agreement, the MESI protocol and its MOESI/MESIF variants, snooping vs directories, what coherence costs, and how false sharing silently destroys multithreaded performance.

lessons.title: DRAM, NUMA and prefetching
lessons.summary: What happens below the last-level cache - DRAM cells, banks and row buffers, timings and bandwidth maths, refresh, NUMA on multi-socket machines, and how hardware and software prefetching hide memory latency.

modules.title: Parallel Hardware
modules.summary: How modern hardware does many things at once: Flynn's taxonomy and the Amdahl and Gustafson limits, multicore memory consistency models (x86-TSO versus ARM), SIMD vectorisation with SSE, AVX and NEON, GPU architecture with warps and SIMT, accelerators such as TPUs and FPGAs, and how to measure performance with perf and the roofline model.

lessons.title: Flynn's taxonomy, Amdahl and Gustafson
lessons.summary: The four classic ways hardware can be parallel, and the two laws that tell you how much faster more cores can actually make a program.

lessons.title: Multicore memory consistency models
lessons.summary: Why cores can see each other's writes in surprising orders, how x86-TSO differs from ARM's weaker model, and how fences and acquire/release atomics restore sanity.

lessons.title: SIMD and vectorisation
lessons.summary: How one instruction can process 4, 8 or 16 values at once with SSE, AVX and NEON, what stops compilers vectorising your loops, and how to write code they can.

lessons.title: GPU architecture: SIMT, warps and memory
lessons.summary: How a GPU runs tens of thousands of threads by grouping them into warps, why branch divergence and uncoalesced memory access hurt, and how the GPU memory hierarchy shapes fast kernels.

lessons.title: Accelerators: TPUs, FPGAs and ASICs
lessons.summary: How specialised hardware can improve efficiency, how a TPU's systolic array multiplies matrices, what FPGAs are good for, and when offloading is worth it.

lessons.title: Measuring performance: perf and the roofline model
lessons.summary: How to benchmark honestly, read hardware counters with perf, find hot spots with sampling profilers, and use the roofline model to compare arithmetic and memory-bandwidth ceilings.

subjects.title: Programming Languages & Compilers
subjects.description: Paradigms, type systems, memory management, functional ideas, compilers and concurrency models.

modules.title: Programming Paradigms
modules.summary: Imperative and declarative styles, object-oriented and functional programming, logic and dataflow languages, multi-paradigm design, and the scope, binding and evaluation rules underneath them all.

lessons.title: Imperative vs declarative
lessons.summary: Telling the machine how versus telling it what, why SQL, React and Kubernetes are declarative, and where the abstraction leaks.

lessons.title: Object-oriented programming
lessons.summary: Encapsulation, inheritance versus composition, polymorphism, and how method dispatch actually works in Java, Python and JavaScript.

lessons.title: Functional programming basics
lessons.summary: Pure functions, immutability, higher-order functions, folds, currying and composition, with the same ideas in Haskell, Python, JavaScript and Java.

lessons.title: Logic and dataflow languages
lessons.summary: Prolog's facts, rules, unification and backtracking, Datalog's comeback in code analysis, and dataflow from spreadsheets to reactive UIs.

lessons.title: Multi-paradigm languages and choosing one
lessons.summary: Why almost every modern language mixes paradigms, the expression problem that decides which style suits which code, and how to choose a language and a style on purpose.

lessons.title: Scope, binding, closures and evaluation strategies
lessons.summary: How languages decide what a name refers to, how closures capture variables, and when and how function arguments get evaluated.

modules.title: Type Systems
modules.summary: What types are for, static versus dynamic and strong versus weak checking, type inference, generics, subtyping and variance, algebraic data types and pattern matching, and the guarantees and trade-offs of gradual typing.

lessons.title: Static vs dynamic, strong vs weak
lessons.summary: What a type actually is, when it gets checked (compile time or run time), how much a language coerces behind your back, and why these are two separate questions.

lessons.title: Type inference (Hindley–Milner intuition)
lessons.summary: How compilers work out types you never wrote, from local inference in Java, Rust and TypeScript to the constraint-and-unification engine of Hindley–Milner in Haskell and OCaml.

lessons.title: Generics and parametric polymorphism
lessons.summary: Writing code once for every type without losing type information, bounded generics, what parametricity guarantees, and how Java, Rust, C#, Haskell, TypeScript and Python actually implement generics.

lessons.title: Subtyping and variance
