lessons.summary: When one type can stand in for another, nominal versus structural subtyping, why functions are contravariant in their arguments, why mutable containers must be invariant, and how Java, TypeScript, Python, Kotlin, C# and Rust express variance.

lessons.title: Algebraic data types and pattern matching
lessons.summary: Building types from "and" and "or", counting their values, replacing null and error codes with Option and Result, and using exhaustive pattern matching in Haskell, Rust, TypeScript, Python and Java to make illegal states unrepresentable.

lessons.title: Gradual typing and soundness
lessons.summary: How TypeScript and Python's type hints add static checking to dynamic languages, what the any type really does, what soundness means and why TypeScript gives it up on purpose, how sound gradual languages enforce types at boundaries, and how to migrate a large codebase.

modules.title: Memory Management & Garbage Collection
modules.summary: How languages decide where values live and when they die: stack and heap, manual memory and its bugs, reference counting, tracing and generational collectors, modern low-pause GCs in Java and Go, and Rust's ownership and borrowing.

lessons.title: Stack vs heap
lessons.summary: Where values live in C, Python, Java, Go and Rust, why the stack is fast but short-lived, and how escape analysis decides what goes on the heap.

lessons.title: Manual memory and its bugs
lessons.summary: The malloc/free contract seen from the programmer's side, the five classic bugs it invites, why they become security holes, and the tools and disciplines (ownership rules, RAII, arenas, sanitizers) that tame them.

lessons.title: Reference counting and cycles
lessons.summary: Freeing an object the moment its last reference disappears, how CPython, Swift, C++ and Rust do it, what it costs, why cycles defeat it, and the weak references and cycle collectors that fix them.

lessons.title: Tracing GC: mark-sweep, copying and generational
lessons.summary: How tracing collectors find live objects from the roots, the three classic designs (mark-sweep, mark-compact and copying), why most objects die young, and how generational collectors with write barriers exploit that.

lessons.title: Modern GCs: G1, ZGC, Go and pause times
lessons.summary: How production collectors shrink pauses by working concurrently with the program, the tri-colour invariant and the barriers that protect it, and how Java's G1 and ZGC and Go's collector make different trade-offs between latency, throughput and memory.

lessons.title: Rust ownership and borrowing
lessons.summary: How Rust frees memory deterministically with no garbage collector and no use-after-free, through single ownership, moves, Drop, shared and mutable borrows, and lifetimes, plus the escape hatches (Rc, RefCell, unsafe) and what it costs to work this way.

modules.title: Functional Programming
modules.summary: Pure functions and immutability, higher-order functions, recursion and tail calls, laziness, functors and monads, and persistent data structures with their performance trade-offs.

lessons.title: Pure functions and immutability
lessons.summary: What makes a function pure, why referential transparency matters, and how immutability works (and leaks) in Python, JavaScript and Haskell.

lessons.title: Higher-order functions, map, filter and reduce
lessons.summary: Functions as values, the map/filter/reduce trio, closures, currying and composition, with the gotchas that bite in Python and JavaScript.

lessons.title: Recursion and tail calls
lessons.summary: How recursion replaces loops, what it costs on the call stack, why tail calls can run in constant space, and which languages actually optimise them.

lessons.title: Laziness
lessons.summary: Evaluating only what is needed, when it is needed - thunks, infinite structures, generators in Python and JavaScript, Haskell's call-by-need, and the space leaks and surprises laziness brings.

lessons.title: Functors and monads, explained practically
lessons.summary: What map and flatMap really do, why "a value in a box" is a useful pattern, and how Optional, Result, lists, Promises and async/await are all the same idea in disguise.

lessons.title: Persistent data structures
lessons.summary: How immutable lists, trees, maps and vectors make cheap "modified copies" by sharing structure, the 32-way tries behind Clojure, Scala and Immutable.js, and the traps where persistence breaks amortised bounds.

modules.title: Compilers & Interpreters
modules.summary: How source text becomes running code: lexing, parsing, ASTs and symbol tables, IR and SSA optimisation, code generation and register allocation, then bytecode VMs and JITs like V8 and HotSpot, all built around one small expression language.

lessons.title: The compiler pipeline
lessons.summary: What compilers and interpreters actually do, the stages from source text to running code, and the tiny expression language Calc that the rest of this module builds.

lessons.title: Lexing: from regular expressions to DFAs
lessons.summary: How a lexer turns characters into tokens, why maximal munch matters, and how regular expressions become NFAs and then fast DFAs, with a working lexer for Calc.

lessons.title: Parsing: grammars, recursive descent and precedence
lessons.summary: How a parser turns a flat list of tokens into a tree, using grammars, recursive descent and precedence climbing, and how top-down LL parsing compares with bottom-up LR parsers like yacc and Bison.

lessons.title: ASTs, semantic analysis and symbol tables
lessons.summary: How compilers represent programs as abstract syntax trees, walk them with pattern matching and visitors, and use scoped symbol tables to catch undefined names, shadowing and checks beyond this grammar.

lessons.title: IR, SSA and optimisation
lessons.summary: Why compilers lower the AST to an intermediate representation, how three-address code and static single assignment make analysis easy, and how constant folding, algebraic simplification, CSE and dead-code elimination work, with illustrative optimisation passes for Calc.

lessons.title: Code generation and register allocation
lessons.summary: How a back end turns IR into instructions for a stack machine or a real CPU, choosing instructions, mapping unlimited temporaries onto a handful of registers with liveness analysis, linear scan and graph colouring, and spilling when they run out.

lessons.title: Interpreters, bytecode VMs and JIT compilers
lessons.summary: How tree-walking interpreters execute programs, how bytecode VMs and dispatch loops work, and how JIT compilers such as V8, HotSpot and PyPy use profiling, inline caches, speculation and deoptimisation to make dynamic languages fast.

modules.title: Concurrency Models in Languages
modules.summary: How languages let you do many things at once: threads and shared memory, async/await and event loops, coroutines and green threads, CSP channels, actors, and structured concurrency with safe Rust’s compile-time protection against data races.

lessons.title: Threads and shared memory
lessons.summary: The default concurrency model of most languages, why `counter += 1` is not safe, what a language memory model promises, and how locks, atomics and the GIL fit in.

lessons.title: async/await and event loops
lessons.summary: How one thread can juggle thousands of connections, what `await` really does, how Python's asyncio and JavaScript's event loop schedule work, and the classic ways to get it wrong.

lessons.title: Coroutines and green threads
lessons.summary: Functions that can pause and resume, the difference between stackless and stackful coroutines, and how Go, Erlang and Java virtual threads schedule millions of lightweight threads on a handful of OS threads.

lessons.title: CSP, goroutines and channels
lessons.summary: Tony Hoare's idea of independent processes that only talk over channels, as realised in Go, with unbuffered and buffered channels, select, closing, pipelines, worker pools, and the deadlocks and leaks to watch for.

lessons.title: Actors, Erlang and Akka
lessons.summary: The actor model of isolated processes with mailboxes, how Erlang builds fault-tolerant systems from it with links, supervisors and "let it crash", and how Akka and Orleans bring it to the JVM and .NET.

lessons.title: Structured concurrency and Rust's data-race freedom
lessons.summary: Two ideas that make concurrent code checkable - structured concurrency, where tasks cannot outlive the block that started them, and Rust's ownership rules plus Send and Sync, which turn data races into compile errors.

subjects.title: Security & Cryptography
subjects.description: Threat modelling, cryptography, PKI, web vulnerabilities, systems security and secure engineering.

modules.title: Security Fundamentals
modules.summary: The vocabulary and mental models of security: the CIA triad and AAA, threat modelling with STRIDE and attack trees, design principles, authentication, access control models and how real intrusions unfold.

lessons.title: The CIA triad and AAA
lessons.summary: What "secure" actually means (confidentiality, integrity, availability) and the authentication, authorisation and accounting machinery that enforces it.

lessons.title: Threat modelling with STRIDE and attack trees
lessons.summary: A structured way to ask "what can go wrong?" before attackers do, using data-flow diagrams, STRIDE per element and costed attack trees.

lessons.title: Security design principles
lessons.summary: Least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation and the other Saltzer and Schroeder principles, with the real failures that show why they matter.

lessons.title: Authentication factors and passwords
lessons.summary: Knowledge, possession and inherence factors, why passwords fail, how to store them, modern NIST guidance, and why passkeys resist phishing when one-time codes don't.

lessons.title: Access control models
lessons.summary: DAC, MAC (Bell–LaPadula and Biba), RBAC, ABAC and relationship-based access control, ACLs versus capabilities, and why broken access control tops the OWASP list.

lessons.title: Attacker techniques and the kill chain
lessons.summary: How real intrusions unfold, modelled with the Lockheed Martin kill chain and MITRE ATT&CK, and how defenders use those models to detect and disrupt attacks at every stage.

modules.title: Cryptography Basics
modules.summary: The building blocks: symmetric ciphers and AEAD, hash functions, MACs, RSA and elliptic curves, Diffie–Hellman key exchange, secure randomness, KDFs and password hashing, and why you use vetted libraries rather than rolling your own.

lessons.title: Symmetric encryption
lessons.summary: How AES and its modes work, why ECB leaks patterns and CTR without a MAC is malleable, and why modern code uses AEAD (AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) from a vetted library.

lessons.title: Hash functions and their properties
lessons.summary: What a cryptographic hash guarantees (preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance), the birthday bound, why MD5 and SHA-1 are broken, length extension, and which hash to pick today.

lessons.title: MACs and HMAC
lessons.summary: How message authentication codes prove a message came from a key holder and wasn't altered, why SHA256(key || msg) is broken, how HMAC works, constant-time verification, replay, and encrypt-then-MAC.

lessons.title: Asymmetric encryption
lessons.summary: Public and private keys, a full small-number RSA walkthrough, why textbook RSA is insecure and OAEP is needed, key sizes, hybrid encryption, and the intuition behind elliptic-curve cryptography.

lessons.title: Key exchange and Diffie–Hellman
lessons.summary: How two strangers agree a secret over a public channel, Diffie–Hellman worked with small numbers, the man-in-the-middle attack and why key exchange must be authenticated, small-subgroup and Logjam pitfalls, ECDH with X25519, and forward secrecy.

lessons.title: Randomness, KDFs and password hashing
lessons.summary: Why crypto needs a CSPRNG and what happens when randomness fails, HKDF for deriving keys from strong secrets, and how to store passwords with salted, slow, memory-hard hashes (Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt, PBKDF2).

modules.title: Applied Cryptography & PKI
modules.summary: How the primitives become real systems: digital signatures, certificates and chains of trust, how TLS combines everything, key management with KMS and HSMs, end-to-end encryption in the Signal protocol, and the mistakes and post-quantum changes that shape modern crypto engineering.

lessons.title: Digital signatures
lessons.summary: How a private key produces a signature anyone can check, how signature schemes process messages and why textbook RSA is unsafe, how RSA-PSS, ECDSA and Ed25519 differ, and where signatures quietly hold the internet together.

lessons.title: Certificates and PKI
lessons.summary: How an X.509 certificate binds a name to a public key, how CAs validate domains and build chains of trust, why revocation is hard and certificates are getting shorter, and how Certificate Transparency keeps CAs honest.

lessons.title: How TLS uses all of it
lessons.summary: TLS 1.3 seen as a composition of primitives: ephemeral Diffie–Hellman for keys, signatures and certificates for identity, HKDF and a transcript hash to bind it together, and AEAD with counter nonces for the records.

lessons.title: Key management, HSMs and envelope encryption
lessons.summary: Why the hard part of cryptography is the keys, how HSMs and cloud KMS keep them out of reach, how envelope encryption scales that to petabytes, and how rotation, access control and crypto-shredding work in practice.

lessons.title: End-to-end encryption and the Signal protocol
lessons.summary: What end-to-end encryption promises beyond TLS, how Signal's X3DH/PQXDH handshake works with an offline recipient, how the Double Ratchet gives forward secrecy and break-in recovery, and where E2EE still leaks (keys, groups, devices, metadata, backups).

lessons.title: Common crypto mistakes and post-quantum cryptography
lessons.summary: Common mistakes that cause cryptographic failures (nonce reuse, unauthenticated modes, bad randomness, timing leaks, hand-rolled constructions) and the coming migration to post-quantum algorithms: what Shor and Grover break, the NIST standards, sizes, hybrids and how to plan the move.

modules.title: Web Application Security
modules.summary: How browsers isolate sites and how attackers get around that isolation: the same-origin policy and CORS, XSS and Content Security Policy, and CSRF with SameSite cookies.

lessons.title: The same-origin policy and CORS
lessons.summary: Why your browser stops one site reading another site's data, exactly what counts as an origin, and how CORS grants controlled access and how misconfiguration exposes data.

lessons.title: XSS (stored, reflected, DOM) and CSP
lessons.summary: How attacker-controlled text ends up running as script in your users' browsers, why context-aware output encoding is the real fix, and how a strict Content Security Policy limits the damage when you miss one.

lessons.title: CSRF and SameSite
lessons.summary: Why browsers will happily send your users' cookies on requests that another site started, and the layered defences (tokens, SameSite cookies, Origin and Fetch Metadata checks) that stop it.

modules.title: Systems Security
modules.summary: Memory-safety bugs and layered defences: what each mitigation can protect, its requirements and its limits.

lessons.title: Memory-safety bugs
lessons.summary: Buffer overflows, out-of-bounds reads, use-after-free, double free, integer overflows and format strings, why they are dangerous and how to fix and find them.

lessons.title: Exploit mitigations
lessons.summary: Stack canaries, DEP/NX, ASLR, RELRO, FORTIFY_SOURCE, control-flow integrity, shadow stacks and memory tagging, what each one stops and what it doesn't.

modules.title: Security Engineering in Practice
modules.summary: How security is done day to day: building it into the SDLC, defending the software supply chain, managing secrets, and detecting and responding to incidents, taught through SolarWinds, xz-utils and Log4Shell.

lessons.title: The secure SDLC, SAST and DAST
lessons.summary: Building security into every phase of development rather than bolting it on at the end, and what static analysis, dynamic scanning, dependency scanning and fuzzing each can and cannot find.

lessons.title: Software supply-chain security
lessons.summary: How attackers compromise you through the code you didn't write and the systems that build it, told through SolarWinds, xz-utils and Log4Shell, and the defences that help: lockfiles and hashes, SBOMs, SLSA provenance and signing.

lessons.title: Secrets management
lessons.summary: Where API keys, passwords and tokens should live, why git and environment variables leak them, and how secret stores, short-lived credentials, rotation and OIDC federation shrink the damage when one escapes.

lessons.title: Logging, detection and incident response
lessons.summary: What to log and how to keep it trustworthy, how detection rules and alerting work (and fail), and how to run an incident from first alert to blameless postmortem, with SolarWinds and Log4Shell as case studies.

subjects.title: Software Engineering
subjects.description: Design principles, patterns, testing, Git, architecture and the practices of effective teams.

modules.title: Design Principles & Clean Code
modules.summary: Naming and functions, coupling and cohesion, SOLID, DRY/KISS/YAGNI and where they stop helping, error handling, and writing code, comments and APIs for other people.

lessons.title: Clean code: naming and functions
lessons.summary: Why readable code matters, how to choose names that carry meaning, and how to shape functions that do one thing at one level of abstraction.

lessons.title: Coupling and cohesion
lessons.summary: The two forces behind almost every design decision, the classic scales for measuring them, connascence, the Law of Demeter and how to spot trouble in real code.

lessons.title: SOLID with examples
lessons.summary: The five SOLID principles with before-and-after code in Python and Java, what each one actually says, and where following them blindly does more harm than good.

lessons.title: DRY, KISS, YAGNI and their limits
lessons.summary: What DRY, KISS and YAGNI actually say, why "duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction", the rule of three, and how to tell simple from merely easy.

lessons.title: Error handling
lessons.summary: Classifying failures, exceptions versus result values, Python's try/except/else/finally in depth, chaining, fail-fast validation, and the anti-patterns that turn small faults into outages.

lessons.title: Writing code for others: comments, docs and APIs
lessons.summary: When comments help and when they lie, docstrings and type hints, the four kinds of documentation, commit messages, and designing APIs that are hard to misuse and safe to evolve under Hyrum's Law.

modules.title: Design Patterns
modules.summary: The Gang of Four catalogue as a working engineer uses it: the problem each pattern solves, its structure, idiomatic Python, when not to use it, where it shows up in real libraries, and the anti-patterns to avoid.

lessons.title: Why patterns
lessons.summary: What a design pattern is, where the idea came from, the two principles behind the Gang of Four catalogue, and why many patterns shrink or vanish in a language like Python.

lessons.title: Creational patterns
lessons.summary: Factory method, abstract factory, builder, prototype and singleton, what each solves, how they look in idiomatic Python, when to avoid them, and where real libraries use them.

lessons.title: Structural patterns
lessons.summary: Adapter, decorator, proxy, facade, composite, bridge and flyweight, how to tell the wrappers apart, idiomatic Python for each, and where they live in io, requests, Django and the JDK.

lessons.title: Strategy, observer and command
lessons.summary: Three behavioural patterns you will use weekly, swappable algorithms, change notification and requests as objects, with Python versions, failure modes such as lapsed listeners, and real uses in Django, Qt and the standard library.

lessons.title: State, template method, iterator and visitor
lessons.summary: Objects whose behaviour depends on their state, algorithms with overridable steps, uniform traversal, and operations over a tree of types, with double dispatch, the expression problem and the Python features that replace each pattern.

lessons.title: Anti-patterns
lessons.summary: The recurring bad solutions, from god objects and big balls of mud to golden hammers, lava flows, singleton abuse and pattern overuse, why sensible teams fall into them, how to spot them, and how to climb back out.

modules.title: Testing
modules.summary: Why we test and how to shape a suite: unit tests done well, test doubles, integration, end-to-end and contract tests, TDD, property-based testing, and keeping a suite trustworthy with coverage, mutation testing and a war on flakiness.

lessons.title: Why test, and the test pyramid
lessons.summary: What automated tests buy you, what they can never prove, and how to balance fast unit tests against slower, more realistic integration and end-to-end tests.

lessons.title: Unit testing well
lessons.summary: What a good unit test looks like, the pytest tools that make them easy (assert, raises, approx, parametrize, fixtures), and the habits that keep tests valuable rather than brittle.

lessons.title: Test doubles (mocks, stubs, fakes)
lessons.summary: Dummies, stubs, spies, mocks and fakes, how to use unittest.mock correctly (including where to patch and autospec), and how over-mocking produces tests that pass while production breaks.

lessons.title: Integration and end-to-end tests, contract testing
lessons.summary: Testing your code against real databases and services, keeping integration tests isolated, using a few end-to-end tests well, and catching broken service boundaries with consumer-driven contract tests.

lessons.title: TDD and property-based testing
lessons.summary: The red-green-refactor cycle worked through step by step, what TDD is and isn't good for, and how property-based testing with Hypothesis generates and shrinks inputs to find bugs you would never have thought to test.

lessons.title: Flaky tests, coverage, mutation testing
lessons.summary: Why tests flake and how to find and fix them, what line and branch coverage do and don't tell you, and how mutation testing measures whether your tests would actually catch a bug.

modules.title: Version Control & CI/CD
modules.summary: How Git really stores history, merging versus rebasing, branching workflows, code review, CI pipelines, and continuous delivery with sensible release and versioning practice.

lessons.title: Git's object model
lessons.summary: Blobs, trees, commits and tags, content addressing, refs and HEAD, the index, packfiles, and how reflogs can recover commits while their objects are retained.

lessons.title: Branching, merging vs rebasing
lessons.summary: Fast-forwards, three-way merges and conflicts, rebasing and interactive rebase, squash merges, safe force-pushing, and how to undo each of them.

lessons.title: Workflows (trunk-based, GitFlow)
lessons.summary: Why integration frequency is the variable that matters, how GitHub flow, GitFlow and trunk-based development work, release branches and backports, and how to choose.

lessons.title: Code review
lessons.summary: What review is really for, how big a change should be, what reviewers look for and in what order, writing useful comments, and the process settings that keep review fast.

lessons.title: CI pipelines
lessons.summary: Continuous integration as a practice, how to structure a fast pipeline, testing the merged result with merge queues, flaky tests, build-once artefacts and securing the pipeline itself.

lessons.title: CD, release engineering, semantic versioning
lessons.summary: Continuous delivery versus deployment, separating deploy from release, rolling, blue-green and canary rollouts, safe schema changes, rollback strategy, SemVer and its ranges, automated versioning and the DORA metrics.

modules.title: Software Architecture at the Code Level
modules.summary: How to structure the inside of an application: layers, ports and adapters, domain-driven design, module boundaries and dependency rules, designing APIs and libraries others depend on, and recording and evolving architectural decisions.

lessons.title: Layered architecture
lessons.summary: Splitting an application into presentation, application, domain and data layers, the one rule that makes layering work, and the ways it goes wrong in practice.

lessons.title: Hexagonal and clean architecture
lessons.summary: Ports and adapters, the dependency rule, how clean and onion architecture relate, a working Python example with fakes for testing, and when the extra indirection isn't worth it.

lessons.title: Domain-driven design
lessons.summary: Ubiquitous language, entities and value objects, aggregates as consistency boundaries, domain events, bounded contexts and how they map onto each other.

lessons.title: Modularity and dependency management
lessons.summary: Information hiding and deep modules, drawing module boundaries, Python's tools for public interfaces, the acyclic and stable dependencies principles, breaking import cycles, modular monoliths and managing third-party packages.

lessons.title: API and library design
lessons.summary: Designing interfaces other code depends on, from Python signatures, defaults, errors and return types to Hyrum's law, semantic versioning, what counts as a breaking change and how to deprecate safely.

lessons.title: Architecture decision records and evolutionary architecture
lessons.summary: Writing ADRs that capture why a decision was made, telling reversible decisions from irreversible ones, guarding architecture with fitness functions, and changing structure safely with strangler fig and branch by abstraction.

modules.title: Engineering Practices
modules.summary: The day-to-day craft around the code: refactoring safely, managing technical debt, debugging and profiling methodically, Agile, Scrum, Kanban and honest estimation, and working well in a team through docs, on-call and blameless postmortems.

lessons.title: Refactoring techniques
lessons.summary: What refactoring really is, the safety net it needs, the core moves from Fowler's catalogue, and how to restructure large systems with parallel change, branch by abstraction and the strangler fig.

lessons.title: Technical debt
lessons.summary: Where the debt metaphor comes from, Fowler's four kinds of debt, how to find the debt that is actually costing you, and how to pay it down and argue for it with the business.

lessons.title: Debugging methodically
lessons.summary: Debugging as the scientific method - reproduce, minimise, binary-search the cause with tools like git bisect and pdb, fix the cause rather than the symptom, and handle the nasty cases such as heisenbugs.

lessons.title: Profiling and performance work
lessons.summary: How to make code faster without guessing - set a target, benchmark honestly, use Amdahl's law, read cProfile output and flame graphs, tell CPU time from waiting, and go after the wins that actually matter.

lessons.title: Agile, Scrum, Kanban and estimation
lessons.summary: What the Agile Manifesto actually says, how Scrum and Kanban work and differ, Little's law for flow, and how to estimate and forecast honestly with story points, ranges and Monte Carlo simulation.

lessons.title: Working in teams - docs, review, on-call and postmortems
lessons.summary: The practices that let a team of engineers work as more than the sum of its parts - Conway's law and bus factor, design docs and the four kinds of documentation, effective code review, a sustainable on-call rotation, and blameless postmortems.

subjects.title: Theory & Discrete Maths
subjects.description: Logic, proofs, combinatorics, probability, automata, computability and complexity.

modules.title: Logic & Proofs
modules.summary: Propositional and predicate logic, the core proof techniques, induction, loop invariants for proving code correct, and an introduction to Boolean satisfiability and SAT solvers.

lessons.title: Propositional logic
lessons.summary: Propositions, connectives and truth tables, why "if p then q" behaves the way it does, the equivalences you use to simplify conditions, and valid versus invalid arguments.

lessons.title: Predicate logic and quantifiers
lessons.summary: Predicates, domains and the quantifiers ∀ and ∃, how to translate English and code into them, negating and nesting quantifiers correctly, and where they show up in Big-O, Python and SQL.

lessons.title: Proof techniques (direct, contrapositive, contradiction)
lessons.summary: How to prove a claim rather than test it, using direct proof, contrapositive, contradiction and cases, plus existence proofs, counterexamples and the mistakes that make a proof worthless.

lessons.title: Induction (weak, strong, structural)
lessons.summary: Proving statements about every natural number, every list or every tree with induction, including strong and structural induction, strengthening the hypothesis, and why recursion and induction are the same idea.

lessons.title: Invariants for proving algorithms correct
lessons.summary: Loop invariants and variants, the initialise–maintain–terminate recipe, worked proofs for binary search, fast exponentiation, Euclid's algorithm and insertion sort, and how invariants show up in assertions, data structures and verified systems.

lessons.title: Boolean satisfiability intro
lessons.summary: The SAT problem, conjunctive normal form and how to encode real problems into it, why it is NP-complete while 2-SAT and Horn-SAT are easy, and how DPLL and CDCL solvers handle millions of variables in practice.

modules.title: Discrete Structures
modules.summary: Sets, functions, relations, counting, recurrences, graphs and number theory: the discrete maths underneath data structures, algorithm analysis, databases and cryptography.

lessons.title: Sets and functions
lessons.summary: Set notation and operations, power sets and Cartesian products, injective, surjective and bijective functions, and why infinite sets come in different sizes.

lessons.title: Relations, equivalence classes and partial orders
lessons.summary: Binary relations and their properties, equivalence relations and the partitions they create, partial orders, Hasse diagrams, topological sorting and closures.

lessons.title: Counting: permutations, combinations and pigeonhole
lessons.summary: The sum and product rules, permutations and combinations, repetition and stars and bars, the binomial theorem, and the pigeonhole principle behind hash collisions and impossible compressors.

lessons.title: Inclusion–exclusion, recurrences and generating functions
lessons.summary: Counting overlapping cases with inclusion–exclusion, derangements and surjections, setting up and solving recurrences, and using generating functions to turn counting into polynomial multiplication.

lessons.title: Graph theory essentials
lessons.summary: Degrees and the handshaking lemma, trees, Euler and Hamilton paths, bipartite graphs and colouring, and planarity with Euler's formula, plus where each shows up in real systems.

lessons.title: Number theory for CS
lessons.summary: Modular arithmetic, Euclid's algorithm and its extended form, modular inverses, primes and primality testing, fast exponentiation, Fermat and Euler, and how they combine into RSA.

modules.title: Probability for Computer Science
modules.summary: Sample spaces, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, expectation and linearity, the distributions engineers actually meet, probability inside algorithms (hashing, birthday bounds, randomised quicksort) and the statistics behind latency percentiles and A/B tests.

lessons.title: Probability basics and conditional probability
lessons.summary: Sample spaces, events, the axioms, complements, independence and conditional probability, with the counting tricks and reliability sums engineers use every day.

lessons.title: Bayes' theorem and the base-rate fallacy
lessons.summary: How to turn P(evidence | cause) into P(cause | evidence), how rare events and false-positive rates affect the meaning of an alert, and how naive Bayes spam filters work.

lessons.title: Random variables, expectation and linearity
lessons.summary: Random variables, expected value and variance, and linearity of expectation with indicator variables, the trick behind most average-case analyses in algorithms.

lessons.title: Distributions: binomial, geometric, Poisson, normal
lessons.summary: The four distributions engineers meet most, what process each one models, their means and variances, and how to use them for packet loss, retries, request arrivals, capacity planning and quorums.

lessons.title: Probability in algorithms
lessons.summary: Hash collisions and load factors, the birthday bound behind ID lengths and hash security, randomised quicksort's expected comparisons, Bloom filter false positives, and Las Vegas versus Monte Carlo algorithms.

lessons.title: Statistics for engineers
lessons.summary: Mean versus median, latency percentiles and the tail at scale, standard errors and confidence intervals, and how to run an A/B test without fooling yourself through peeking, multiple comparisons or too small a sample.

modules.title: Automata & Regular Languages
modules.summary: Finite automata, nondeterminism and the subset construction, turning regexes into machines, proving languages non-regular, minimising DFAs, and how real regex engines work and fail.

lessons.title: Deterministic finite automata
lessons.summary: The simplest model of a computer, a machine with a fixed number of states and no memory beyond them, and how it decides which strings belong to a language.

lessons.title: NFAs and the subset construction
lessons.summary: Nondeterministic automata that can be in many states at once, ε-moves, and the subset construction that turns any NFA into an equivalent DFA, sometimes at exponential cost.

lessons.title: From regular expressions to NFAs (Thompson)
lessons.summary: What a regular expression formally is, Thompson's construction for compiling one into an ε-NFA piece by piece, a working Python version, and the reverse trip from automaton back to regex.

lessons.title: The pumping lemma
lessons.summary: Why every long string accepted by a finite automaton contains a loop that can be repeated, and how to turn that into proofs that languages like aⁿbⁿ, palindromes and balanced brackets are not regular.

lessons.title: DFA minimisation and Myhill–Nerode
lessons.summary: Which states of a DFA are really the same, the partition-refinement and table-filling algorithms that merge them, the Myhill–Nerode theorem behind them, and what minimal DFAs are used for.

lessons.title: Practical regex engines and ReDoS
lessons.summary: How Perl-style backtracking engines and automaton-based engines like RE2 actually match, why one can take exponential time on a 30-character input, the outages this caused, and how to defend against it.

modules.title: Context-Free Languages & Computability
modules.summary: Beyond finite automata: context-free grammars and pushdown automata, Turing machines, the Church–Turing thesis, and the hard limits of computation proved by diagonalisation, the halting problem, reductions and Rice's theorem.

lessons.title: Context-free grammars
lessons.summary: Grammars that can count and nest, how derivations and parse trees work, ambiguity, Chomsky normal form and the CYK parsing algorithm.

lessons.title: Pushdown automata and the CFL pumping lemma
lessons.summary: A finite automaton plus a stack recognises exactly the context-free languages; the pumping lemma proves that some languages, like aⁿbⁿcⁿ, are beyond them.

lessons.title: Turing machines
lessons.summary: The simplest model of a general-purpose computer, a finite control with a read-write tape, and why it can do what PDAs cannot, simulated in Python down to the busy beaver.

lessons.title: The Church–Turing thesis
lessons.summary: Why standard models of effective computation agree with the Turing machine, what Turing completeness really requires, and the universal machine behind every interpreter.

lessons.title: The halting problem and diagonalisation
lessons.summary: Cantor's diagonal argument shows most problems have no algorithm at all; the same trick proves no program can decide whether programs halt.

lessons.title: Reductions and Rice's theorem
lessons.summary: How to prove a new problem undecidable by transforming a known one into it, and Rice's theorem, which says every non-trivial question about what a program computes is undecidable.

modules.title: Complexity Theory
modules.summary: P, NP and the P vs NP question, NP-completeness and Cook–Levin, worked reductions, coping with NP-hardness, space complexity and PSPACE, and the randomised and quantum classes BPP and BQP, with a clear line between what is proven and what is conjectured.

lessons.title: P and NP
lessons.summary: What "efficient" means, the classes P, NP and coNP defined by solving versus checking, what is proven about them and why P vs NP is still open.

lessons.title: NP-completeness and Cook–Levin
lessons.summary: Polynomial-time reductions, what NP-hard and NP-complete mean, how the Cook–Levin theorem encodes any NP computation as a SAT formula, and the SAT to 3-SAT step that opens the door to Karp's 21 problems.

lessons.title: Reductions in practice
lessons.summary: Worked polynomial-time reductions with concrete instances checked in Python, 3-SAT to Independent Set, Independent Set to Vertex Cover and Clique, Vertex Cover to Set Cover, and the mistakes that make a reduction invalid.

lessons.title: Coping with NP-hardness
lessons.summary: What to do when your problem is NP-hard, with special cases, smarter exponential algorithms, approximation algorithms and their limits (PCP, Unique Games), parameterised algorithms and kernels, and the heuristics and solvers used in industry.

lessons.title: Space complexity and PSPACE
lessons.summary: Measuring memory instead of time, the classes L, NL and PSPACE, Savitch's theorem, NL = coNL, TQBF and games as PSPACE-complete problems, and which separations are proven.

lessons.title: Randomised and quantum complexity
lessons.summary: RP, coRP, ZPP and BPP, error amplification, Freivalds and polynomial identity testing, the conjecture that P = BPP, and BQP with what Shor and Grover do and don't show, keeping proven results apart from beliefs.

subjects.title: Databases & SQL
subjects.description: Writing SQL well, relational theory, normalisation and how queries are actually executed.

modules.title: SQL Fundamentals
modules.summary: Writing correct SQL against one small shop schema: filtering and sorting, inner, outer and cross joins, grouping and aggregates, NULL's three-valued logic, changing data safely with constraints, and designing tables with DDL.

lessons.title: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
lessons.summary: Reading data with SQL. Pick columns, filter rows, sort and page through them, and learn the order in which a query is actually evaluated.

lessons.title: Joins
lessons.summary: Inner, left, right, full, self and cross joins with real result tables, plus the two classic bugs, filtering in WHERE instead of ON and row fan-out.

lessons.title: GROUP BY, HAVING and aggregates
lessons.summary: Turning rows into totals. COUNT, SUM and AVG, grouping rules, WHERE versus HAVING, conditional aggregation, and the join fan-out that silently doubles your numbers.

lessons.title: NULL semantics
lessons.summary: NULL means unknown, not empty. Three-valued logic, why = NULL never matches, the NOT IN trap, and how NULL behaves in aggregates, sorting, constraints and joins.

lessons.title: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and constraints
lessons.summary: Changing data safely. Writing inserts, updates and deletes, wrapping risky changes in a transaction, and letting NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and foreign keys reject bad data for you.

lessons.title: Schema design and DDL
lessons.summary: Designing tables that stay correct for years. Modelling relationships, choosing types and keys, writing CREATE TABLE in SQLite and PostgreSQL, and changing a live schema without downtime.

modules.title: Advanced SQL
modules.summary: The SQL that separates competent from fluent: subqueries and correlation, CTEs and recursion, window functions, set operations and pivots, the classic interview problems, and JSON and upserts, with worked examples and PostgreSQL/SQLite differences called out.

lessons.title: Subqueries and correlated subqueries
lessons.summary: Queries inside queries, from scalar and IN subqueries to correlated EXISTS, the NOT IN NULL trap, and how Postgres actually executes them.

lessons.title: CTEs and recursive CTEs
lessons.summary: Naming intermediate results with WITH, how Postgres and SQLite decide whether to inline or materialise them, and recursive CTEs for hierarchies, series and graph walks.

lessons.title: Window functions
lessons.summary: Computing across related rows without collapsing them, with ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG and LEAD, running totals, moving averages, and the frame rules that trip everyone up.

lessons.title: Set operations and pivoting
lessons.summary: Combining result sets with UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT (and the precedence rule SQLite gets differently), then turning rows into columns and back with conditional aggregation, FILTER, ROLLUP and LATERAL.

lessons.title: Common interview SQL problems
lessons.summary: The handful of patterns behind most SQL interview questions, from Nth highest and top-N per group to relational division, de-duplication, gaps and islands, and medians, with the edge cases interviewers probe.

lessons.title: JSON in SQL, upserts
lessons.summary: Storing and querying JSON in SQLite and PostgreSQL (json vs jsonb, operators, GIN and expression indexes), then atomic insert-or-update with ON CONFLICT, MERGE and RETURNING, and the traps in each.

modules.title: Relational Theory & Normalisation
modules.summary: The maths underneath SQL: relations and keys, relational algebra, functional dependencies and their closures, normal forms from 1NF to BCNF with real decompositions, when to denormalise, and turning a messy domain into a sound ER model.

lessons.title: The relational model
lessons.summary: Relations, tuples, domains and keys as Codd defined them, the integrity rules that follow, and the places where SQL tables quietly break the theory.

lessons.title: Relational algebra
lessons.summary: Selection, projection, joins, set operators and division as operators on relations, how SQL maps onto them, and why algebraic rewrites are the basis of every query optimiser.

lessons.title: Functional dependencies, closure and keys
lessons.summary: What a functional dependency really claims, Armstrong's axioms, the attribute-closure algorithm, finding every candidate key, and computing a minimal cover.

lessons.title: Normal forms from 1NF to BCNF
lessons.summary: Update anomalies and why they happen, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF defined through functional dependencies, lossless and dependency-preserving decomposition, and the BCNF and 3NF algorithms worked by hand.

lessons.title: Denormalisation trade-offs
lessons.summary: When storing redundant data is worth it, the main techniques (copied columns, counters, summary tables, materialised views, star schemas, embedded documents), how to keep copies in sync, and the failure modes.

lessons.title: ER modelling
lessons.summary: Entities, relationships, cardinality and participation, the rules for mapping an ER model to tables, weak entities, ternary relationships, inheritance mappings and the polymorphic-association trap.

modules.title: Query Processing & Optimisation
modules.summary: What happens between sending SQL and getting rows back: parsing, planning and execution, the iterator model, join algorithms, statistics and cost estimation, reading illustrative PostgreSQL EXPLAIN plans, and tuning queries and indexes.

lessons.title: How a query executes
lessons.summary: The journey from SQL text to rows. Parsing, rewriting, planning and execution, the plan tree, the iterator model that streams rows between operators, and why the page is the unit of cost.

lessons.title: Join algorithms and their costs
lessons.summary: Nested loop, hash and merge joins. How each one works, what it costs in page reads, when each wins, and what they look like in real PostgreSQL plans.

lessons.title: Statistics and the cost-based optimiser
lessons.summary: How the planner guesses row counts from pg_stats, turns them into costs, and searches the space of join orders. Worked selectivity calculations, the independence assumption, extended statistics and stale stats.

lessons.title: Reading EXPLAIN plans (Postgres)
lessons.summary: How to read PostgreSQL EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output field by field, find where the time really went, spot misestimates, and recognise the red flags that point to a fix.

lessons.title: Index tuning
lessons.summary: Designing indexes for the queries you actually run. When the planner will use an index, column order in composite indexes, Postgres 18 skip scan, covering and partial indexes, expression indexes, bitmap scans, and what every index costs you.

lessons.title: Common performance anti-patterns
lessons.summary: The query shapes that defeat the planner. Non-sargable predicates, type mismatches, OFFSET pagination, NOT IN, correlated subqueries, DISTINCT as a join fix, OR across columns, N+1 queries, generic plans and exact counts, each with an illustrative plan and a possible rewrite.

modules.title: PostgreSQL
modules.summary: A practical guide to Postgres: architecture, schema design, transactions, JSONB, indexing, vacuum, replication and recovery.

lessons.title: PostgreSQL in practice
lessons.summary: Build a small Postgres database, reason about concurrent writes, choose indexes and understand the maintenance and recovery work behind a reliable service.

subjects.title: Synth Building
subjects.description: Foundations for building a hardware synthesiser: sound and sampling, synthesis DSP, electronics, embedded audio, and MIDI/studio integration.

modules.title: Sound & Digital Audio
modules.summary: The maths and physics a synth builder needs before writing an oscillator: waves, pitch, sampling, aliasing, decibels and headroom, and how to measure audio offline with Python.

lessons.title: Sound as a wave
lessons.summary: Amplitude, frequency, period, wavelength and phase; the sine formula x(t) = A·sin(2πft + φ); and the two numbers every oscillator needs, samples per period and phase increment.

lessons.title: Pitch and tuning
lessons.summary: Octaves, semitones and equal temperament; MIDI note numbers and f = 440·2^((n−69)/12); cents and detuning; why pitch is logarithmic; and the difference between pitch and timbre.

lessons.title: Sampling and quantisation
lessons.summary: How a continuous signal becomes a list of numbers. Sample rate, bit depth, quantisation noise and the 6 dB-per-bit rule, integer vs floating-point samples, and the −1..1 convention.

lessons.title: Nyquist and aliasing
lessons.summary: The sampling theorem and the Nyquist frequency, how to calculate where an alias lands, why sharp synth waveforms alias, and what anti-aliasing and reconstruction filters do.

lessons.title: Level, decibels and headroom
lessons.summary: Amplitude and power decibels, dBFS, peak vs RMS and crest factor, what happens when you sum signals, hard and soft clipping, and how to stage gain inside a digital synth.

lessons.title: Measuring audio offline
lessons.summary: A Python workbench for checking audio by numbers, not just by ear. Generate test signals, plot them, read a spectrum with numpy's FFT, verify frequency and level, confirm an aliasing prediction, and write a WAV file with a library.

modules.title: Synthesis & DSP
modules.summary: How a synth voice turns numbers into sound: synthesis approaches, phase-accumulator oscillators, harmonics, band-limited waveforms, envelopes and smoothing, filters and modulation, with offline Python experiments.

lessons.title: Synthesis approaches and signal flow
lessons.summary: The main ways synths make sound (subtractive, additive, FM/PM, wavetable, sample-based, physical modelling), the classic subtractive voice, and how mono and poly synths allocate voices.

lessons.title: Oscillators and the phase accumulator
lessons.summary: How a digital oscillator keeps track of phase across audio blocks, turns frequency into a phase increment, shapes sine, saw, square, triangle and pulse waves, wraps phase correctly and avoids precision drift.

lessons.title: Harmonics, spectra and timbre
lessons.summary: Why a sawtooth sounds different from a square or triangle at the same pitch, the 1/n and 1/n² harmonic patterns that define them, and how to check them yourself with numpy's FFT.

lessons.title: Band-limited oscillators
lessons.summary: Why naive saw and square oscillators alias, worked out with real numbers, and the established fixes (additive, mipmapped wavetables, oversampling, BLIT, BLEP and PolyBLEP), with a measured PolyBLEP-versus-naive comparison in Python.

lessons.title: Envelopes and parameter smoothing
lessons.summary: ADSR envelopes with linear and exponential (one-pole) segments, retriggering, clicks and legato, plus parameter smoothing to remove zipper noise and how to choose smoothing times.

lessons.title: Filters
lessons.summary: Frequency response, cutoff, slope, resonance and Q; the one-pole low-pass in full (difference equation, coefficient, state, measured response, stability); IIR versus FIR; and a conceptual tour of the biquad, state-variable and ladder filters used in synths.

lessons.title: Modulation, LFOs and the modulation matrix
lessons.summary: LFO rates, shapes and polarity; vibrato and tremolo with correct depth units; envelope and velocity modulation of the filter; a modulation matrix; and the trade-offs of control-rate versus audio-rate modulation.

modules.title: Electronics for Synth Builders
modules.summary: Low-voltage DC electronics for building a synth: Ohm's law, dividers and pots, components, logic levels and datasheets, schematics and breadboards, measurement and soldering, and keeping audio quiet. No mains work.

lessons.title: Voltage, current, resistance and power
lessons.summary: The four quantities behind every circuit, Ohm's law and P = VI, unit prefixes, ground as a reference, complete circuits, and which way current "flows".

lessons.title: Series, parallel and voltage dividers
lessons.summary: Combining resistors, the voltage divider formula, why loading a divider changes its output, and how a knob on a synth is just a divider with a moving tap.

lessons.title: Components: resistors, capacitors, LEDs, diodes, switches and connectors
lessons.summary: The parts in every synth build. How to read their values and ratings, size an LED resistor, use the RC time constant, respect polarity, and check connector pinouts.

lessons.title: Power, logic levels and datasheets
lessons.summary: 3.3 V versus 5 V, logic thresholds and noise margins, absolute maximum ratings versus recommended operating conditions, how to read a datasheet, protecting inputs, and why every chip needs a decoupling capacitor.

lessons.title: Schematics and breadboarding
lessons.summary: Reading schematic symbols and nets, how a solderless breadboard is connected inside, translating a schematic into wiring, documenting it so you can rebuild it, and the checks to make before applying power.

lessons.title: Measurement and soldering
lessons.summary: Using a multimeter correctly (parallel voltage, series current, unpowered resistance and continuity, ranges and fuses), what an oscilloscope adds, and safe, reliable soldering, including how to inspect a joint.

lessons.title: Noise and grounding in audio circuits
lessons.summary: Why audio picks up hum and whine, how ground loops form in a studio, shared-impedance coupling and star grounding, keeping digital return currents out of analogue grounds, shielded cable, and why supply noise and decoupling matter.

modules.title: Embedded Audio & Interfaces
modules.summary: How synth firmware runs on real hardware: microcontrollers and the flash/debug cycle, buttons, knobs, codecs and I2S, serial buses and MIDI's UART, the real-time audio callback and its budget, safe control-to-audio data transfer, and a method for comparing Daisy, Teensy and Raspberry Pi platforms.

lessons.title: Microcontrollers and firmware
lessons.summary: What a microcontroller is, how firmware differs from an application, the build-flash-run-debug cycle, bootloaders, DFU, SWD/JTAG probes, recovering a board, and the three broad hardware approaches for a synth.

lessons.title: GPIO and buttons
lessons.summary: Digital inputs and outputs, pull-up and pull-down resistors, active-low buttons, why switches bounce and four debouncing algorithms, and driving LEDs within a pin's current limits.

lessons.title: ADCs and knobs
lessons.summary: How an ADC turns a knob's voltage into a number, why the reading jitters, how to smooth it with moving averages, one-pole filters and hysteresis, how to map it to musical parameters, and how to read many knobs through a multiplexer.

lessons.title: DACs, codecs and audio I/O
lessons.summary: How samples leave the MCU and become a line-level signal - DACs versus codecs, I2S framing and clocks, sample formats, configuring a codec over I2C, DMA double buffering, and the output stage at a conceptual level.

lessons.title: Serial buses: UART, I2C and SPI
lessons.summary: The three serial buses found in every synth - UART (and why MIDI is a 31,250-baud UART), I2C (addresses, open-drain pull-ups, speed modes) and SPI (clock modes, chip select) - and which one to use for displays, codecs, MIDI and expanders.

lessons.title: The real-time audio model
lessons.summary: How interrupts drive the audio callback, how block size sets the processing budget (with worked numbers), why that budget is not the same as end-to-end latency, what must never happen inside the callback and why, and how to measure CPU load with cycle counters and a scope.

lessons.title: Getting control data to the audio code
lessons.summary: How knob values and MIDI events cross safely from the foreground to the audio callback - why volatile is not synchronisation, atomic single values, single-producer/single-consumer ring buffers, event queues for notes, and smoothing parameters on the receiving side.

lessons.title: Comparing synth platforms
lessons.summary: A method for evaluating a Daisy Seed, a Teensy 4.x with its audio adaptor and a Raspberry Pi with an audio HAT against the project's own criteria, using only official documentation, with model, revision and date recorded. A comparison approach, not a recommendation.

modules.title: MIDI & Studio Integration
modules.summary: MIDI from the byte level up, robust MIDI handling in a synth, MIDI and USB hardware connections, audio levels and safe connections, and wiring the synth into a Digitakt, audio interface and Ableton studio.

lessons.title: MIDI fundamentals
lessons.summary: What MIDI actually carries (events, not audio), the MIDI 1.0 byte format, channels, note on/off, velocity and the note-on-with-velocity-0 rule, worked at the byte level.

lessons.title: The rest of the MIDI message set
lessons.summary: Control change (common numbers and 14-bit pairs), program change, pitch bend, aftertouch, running status, real-time clock and transport, SysEx, and an overview of MIDI 2.0.

lessons.title: Handling MIDI inside a synth
lessons.summary: Parsing a MIDI byte stream robustly with a state machine, note priority for a monophonic synth, preventing stuck notes, and mapping CC values to synth parameters without zipper noise.

lessons.title: MIDI hardware connections
lessons.summary: 5-pin DIN wiring and the 5 mA current loop, why MIDI inputs use an optocoupler, the 3.3 V-capable reference circuit from the MIDI electrical spec, TRS type A versus type B, and USB MIDI host and device roles.

lessons.title: Audio levels and connections
lessons.summary: Mic, instrument, line, headphone and speaker levels and why they aren't interchangeable; −10 dBV versus +4 dBu with the voltage maths; balanced and unbalanced lines, TRS and TS, impedance bridging, DC offset and output coupling, and how to connect a DIY synth to an interface safely.

lessons.title: Integrating with a Digitakt, an interface and Ableton
lessons.summary: Designing the connection diagram (MIDI, audio, power, USB host), sequencing the synth from Digitakt MIDI tracks, recording into Ableton, monitoring and latency, gain staging, and finding and fixing ground loops.

modules.title: Audio Engineering
modules.summary: What happens to your synth's signal after it leaves the jack: acoustics and hearing, microphones, loudspeaker drivers and enclosures, crossovers, power amplifiers, live and studio sound systems, and the room you listen in.

lessons.title: Acoustics and sound in air
lessons.summary: Sound as pressure waves, the speed of sound and wavelength, dB SPL with its 20 µPa reference, the inverse square law with worked maths, adding incoherent sources, and how reflection, absorption and diffraction depend on wavelength.

lessons.title: Hearing and psychoacoustics
lessons.summary: The range of human hearing, equal-loudness contours (ISO 226), A and C weighting, masking and critical bands, how we localise sound with time and level differences, the precedence (Haas) effect, and the exposure limits that protect your hearing.

lessons.title: Microphones
lessons.summary: How dynamic, condenser and ribbon microphones turn pressure into voltage, polar patterns and the maths behind them, proximity effect, reading sensitivity and self-noise specifications, 48 V phantom power (IEC 61938), and placement including the 3:1 rule.

lessons.title: Loudspeaker drivers
lessons.summary: How a moving-coil driver turns current into sound, the real impedance curve behind the "8 Ω" label, sensitivity at 1 W/1 m and 2.83 V/1 m with the maths linking amplifier power to SPL, frequency response, power handling, driver types from woofer to compression driver and horn, and cone breakup.

lessons.title: Enclosure design
lessons.summary: Why a bare driver makes almost no bass, baffle step, sealed, ported, open-baffle and transmission-line designs, Thiele–Small parameters (Fs, Qts, Vas) and the sealed-box equations, Helmholtz port tuning, cabinet resonance and bracing, and what an alignment is.

lessons.title: Crossovers
lessons.summary: Why multi-way speakers split the signal, passive vs active vs DSP crossovers, filter order and slope, why Butterworth crossovers bump and Linkwitz–Riley LR4 sums flat, driver offset and phase, and a worked first-order passive crossover with the reasons it doesn't behave as calculated.

lessons.title: Power amplifiers
lessons.summary: What a power amplifier does, voltage gain versus power, classes A, AB and D with their efficiency and trade-offs, honest power ratings (and why PMPO is meaningless), load impedance and matching an amp to a speaker, damping factor, clipping and tweeter damage, and headphone amplifiers. Conceptual only, with no opening of mains equipment.

lessons.title: Sound systems and signal flow
lessons.summary: The chain from source to listener, the mixing console's channel strip, sends, inserts, buses and subgroups, gain staging across a whole system, PA design with mains, subs, monitors and delay speakers, DI boxes, preventing acoustic feedback, and how studio and live systems differ.

lessons.title: Room acoustics and monitoring
lessons.summary: Room modes and the c/2L axial-mode formula with worked examples, reverberation and RT60 with Sabine's equation, absorption vs diffusion, bass traps, early reflections and the mirror trick, near-field monitor placement (equilateral triangle, wall distance, SBIR), and measuring a room with REW.
